XLV. Provided always, and be it further enacted, That if any such Person who shall have or keep, or cause to be had or kept, any Fire, Candle, or Lamp lighted on board any such Ship or Vessel aforesaid cannot be discovered, then and in such Case the Master, or Owner or Owners of such Ship or Vessel, shall be and is hereby declared tobesubject and liable to the aforesaid Penalty of Five Pounds.

XLVI. And, the better to make known the several Times when Fires and Candles shall beextinguished, as before directed, be it further enacted, That every Evening and Morning, at the Hours herein for the above Purposes appointed, a large Bell to be provided by the said Commissioners shall be rung for the Space of Ten Minutes at lealt, in the said Docks or Basons, or some of them, or in some Place contiguous or near adjoining thereto.

XLVII. And be it further enacted, ThatnoPitch, Tar, Rosin, Turpentine,* Oil, or other combustible Matter, shall, at any Time hereafter, be boiled or heated on board any Ship or other Vessel, Lighter, Craft, or Boac lying in the said Harbour, Dock or Docks, Bason or Basons, or other Works, or any of them, nor in any Place or Places within the said Dock or Bason, except in such Place or Places, and in such Manner, as shall be especially appointed by the said Commissioners, or any Seven or more of them, for that Purpose; nor shall any Gunpowder, or loaded Gun whatever, be brought into the said Docks, Basons, or Pier, or be suffered to remain on board any Ship or any other Vessel, or tipon the Quays or Wharfs, upon Pain that every Master, Commander, or Owner of every Ship or Vessel, so offending in Manner as aforesaid, shall forfeit for every Offence the Sum of Twenty Pounds.

XLVIII. And be it further enacted, That when any Action or Suit shall be brought by Order of the said Commissioners again!! any Person or Persons in pursuance or by virtue of this Act, the fame may be brought in the Name of their Clerk or Treasurer on Behalf of the said Commissioners; and that no such Action or Suit shall abate or be discontinued by the Death or Removal of such Clerk or Treasurer, or by the Act of such Clerk or Treasurer, without the Consent of the said Commissioners for the Time being.

XLIX. Provided always, That all Costs and Expences which shall be incurred, by or on the Behalf of the said Commissioners, or any Person or Persons employed by them in prosecuting or defending any Action or Suit, or Prosecution, touching the Execution of this Act, shall always be reimbursed and paid out of the Monies to be raised by virtue of this Act.

L. And be it further enacted, That no Ship or Vessel, shall upon any Account or Pretence whatsoever, be moored in the said Pier of Southampton, to be used as or in the Nature of a Siorehouse, under the Penalty of Ten Pounds for every Week that the same shall be used for that Purpose, to be paid to the said Commissioners by the Owners or other Person or Persons having the Direction or Charge of such Ship or Vessel.

43° GEORGII III. Cap. 21.

LI. Provided always, That nothing herein contained shall extend, or be construed to extend to hinder the Mayor, Bailiffs, and Burgesses of the said Town and County for the Time being, and their Successors, from receiving and recovering all such Arrears of Petty Customs, Wharfage, Anchorage, and Groundage as shall remain due and unpaid to them before the said Second Monday after the passing this Act.

LII. Provided always, and be it further enacted, That nothing in this Act contained shall extend, or be construed to extend to affect, prejudice, alter, abridge, or take away any Rights, Eftatts, Powers, Immunities, and Advantages or Privileges whatsoever, belonging or appertaining to the Mayor and Corporation of the said ToWn and County, or to any other Person or Persons whomsoever (except such as are hereby expressly taken away or altered), but that all such Rights, Estates, Powers, and Privileges shall continue in full Force and Effect, and may be exercised and enjoyed in as full and ample a Manner to all Intents and Purposes as if this Act had not been made; any Thing herein contained to the contrary notwithstanding.

LIII. And be it further enacted, That all Penalties and Forfeitures by this Act imposed, concerning which no particular Direction hath been already given, shall, if the fame be not paid within Fourteen Days afrer the same shall have been demanded, be recovered and levied by Distress and Sale of the Goods and Chattels of the Offender or Offenders, by Warrant under the Hands and Seals of any Two or more Justices of the Peace for the Town and County of Southampton-, which Warrant they are hereby empowered and required to grant, upon the Information of One or more credible Witness or Witnesses, upon Oath before them made, which Oath they are hereby empowered to administer, provided the Offender or Offenders shall not, in the mean Time, have compounded or settled with the said Commissioners, which they are hereby empowered to do; and that all such Penalties and Forfeitures, and also all other Penalties and Forfeitures by this Act imposed, shall, when recovered (after deducting all Damages and Rewards for the Prosecution of Offenders, and the Costs and Charges of Suit, and rendering the Overplus (if any) when demanded, to the Parties whole Goods and Chattels shall be fib distrained and fold, the Costs and Charges of such Distress and Sale being first deducted, in case the same shall exceed the Sum of Forty Shillings be paid to and for the Purposes of this Act; and in case no such Distress as aforesaid can be had, then it shall and may be lawful for the said Two or more Justices, by like Warrant or Warrants, to commit the Party or Parties offending to the Common Gaol of the Town and County of Southampton, or House of Correction, for the Space of Thirty Days, without Bail or Mainprize, or for any less Time, at the Discretion of such Justices, unless the said Penalty and Charges shall be sooner paid and laiisfied.

LV. Provided always, and be it further enacted, That it shall and may be lawful for the said Justices of the Peace, or any Two of them, by whom any Judgement, Sentence, or Determination, shall be given, pronounced, or made, from Time to Time, when they fee Cause, to mitigate, compound, or lelTen, any of the Penalties or Forfeitures as aforesaid, as he or they, in his or their Discretion, shall think fit, so as such Mitigation or Composition do not extend to remit aboveThreeFourth Parts of the Penalty inflicted and directed to be levied by this Act! \ and that every such Mitigation or Composition shall be a sufficient Discharge for the Persons offending respectively for so much of the said Penalties and Forfeitures as shall be so mitigated, lelfened, or remitted.

LVI. And be it further enacted, That if any Person or Persons shall think him, her, or themselves aggrieved, or remain unsatisfied with the Judgement of the said Justices, or any of them, by reason of any Sentence or Judgement to be given or pronounced by them or any of them as aforesaid, or by any other Matter or Thing done by virtue of this Act, such Person or Persons shall and may complain or appeal to the Justices of the Peace, at the next General Quarter Sessions of the Peace to be held in and for the Town and County of Southampton, first giving Ten Days Notice of such Complaint or Appeal to the Person or Persons against whom such Complaint is intended to be made, who are hereby empowered to summon and examine Witnesses upon Oath, and finally to hear and determine the Matter of every such Complaint or Appeal; and in case of Conviction, to issue a Warrant or Warrants for the levying and enforcing Payment of the said Penalties and Forfeitures, by the Ways and Means before mentioned, together with such Costs and Charges to the Party in whose Favour such Appeal shall be determined as the Justices, in their said Sessions, shall order and direct; which Orders and Judgements relptctively shall be final and condusive to all Parties, and shall not be removed or rc-moveable, by any Writ or Writs of Certiorari or otherwise, into any of His Majesty's Coutts of Record at Westminster or elsewhere.

LVII. And be it further enacted, That all the Costs Charges, and Expences of passing this Act, and incident to the applying for and obtaining thereof, or incurred in relation thereto, and in putting the fame into Execution, shall be borne, paid, and defrayed out of the First Monies which shall be raised by virtue of this Act.

LVIII. And be it further enacted, That no Order, Conviction. Judgement, Warrant, or other Proceedings before Justices of the Peace, to be had or made in pursuance of this Act, shall be quathed or vacated for want of Form; and that in all Cases where any Distress shall be made for any Sum or Sums of Money, to be levied by virtue of this Act, the Distress itself shall not be deemed to be unlawful, nor shall the Parties making the same

LIX. And be it further enacted, That no Proceeding to be had touching the Conviction of any Offender or Offenders against this Act, or any Order made, or other Matter or Thing to be done or transacted in or relating to the Execution of this Act, shall be removed by Certiorari or any other Writ or Process whatsoever into any of His Majesty's Courts of Record at Westminster; any Law or Statute to the contrary in anywise notwithstanding.

LX. And be it further enacted, That no Action at Law shall be commenced against any Person or Persons for any Thing done or to be done by virtue of this Act, until after Fourteen Days Notice thereof shall have been given or left at the ul'ual Place of Abode of the Person or Persons against whom such Action is intended to be brought thereby setting forth the particular Cause of such Action, nor after Tender of sufficicnc Amends hath been made to the Party or Parties aggrieved, nor after Three Calendar Months next after the Fadt commuted, or Cause of such Action shall have arisen; and in every such Action the Venue shall be laid in the Town and County of Southampton, or the next adjoining County, and not elsewhere, and shall not be changed; and the Deiendant or Defendants in every such Action, shall or may plead the General Issue, and give this Act, and the special Matter in Evidence at any Trial to be had thereupon, and that the fame was done by virtue, and under the Authority of this Act , and if upon the Trial of such Action, it shall appear to have been lo done, or that such Action shall be brought before the Expiration of Fourteen Days next after such Notice shall have been given or left as aforesaid, or after sufficient Tender of Amends shall have been made to the Party or Parties aggrieved, or after the End of Three Calendar Months next after the Fast committed, or Cause of such Action shall have arisen, or if the Venue in such Action shall be laid otherve lie than as aforesaid, then and in every of the said Cases the Jury on the Trial of Inch Action or Actions shall find a Verdict for the Defendant or Defendants therein; and in all Cases wherein a Verdict shall be found for any Defendant or Defendants in any such Action, or the Plaintiff or Plaintiffs therein shall discontinue the lame after the Defendant or Defendants shall have appeared thereto, or shall be nonsuited; or if upon [Loc. GEORGII III. REGIS.

Cap. 22.

An Act for altering and amending the several Laws now in force, for enabling The Royal Canal Company to complete a Navigable Canal from Dublin to Tarmonbury on the River Shannon.

[7th April 1803.]

WHEREAS by an Act made in the Parliament of Ireland, in the Twenty-ninth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, An Act for the Promotion and Encouragement of Inland Navigation, it is enacted, that so soon as any of the Subscribers to any of the Undertakings therein mentioned should be constituted and created into a Body Corporate, they should be and Hand inverted with and hold and enjoy all and Angular the like Powers, Privileges, Advantages, and Authorities in all Things, for the Purposes of carrying on the Navigation, and of Branches therein mentioned, as were before the parting of that Act verted in the Corporation for promoting and carrying on an Inland Navigation in Ireland, and as were then verted in the Company of Undertakers of the Grand Canal for the Purpose of enabling them to carry on the said Canal: And whereas certain Persons having subscribed to an Undertaking for completing a Navigable Canal from Dublin to Tarmon-[Loc. and be it enacted by the King’s most Excellent Majesty, by and with the Advice and Consent of the Lords Spiritual and lemporal, and Commons, in this present Parliament assembled, and by the Authority of the Directois. fame, That a General Assembly of the said Company of Proprietors shall be holden on the Fourth Monday after the passing of this Act, for the Purpose of electing Fifteen Directors for the Management of the Affairs of the said Company; and the said Company shall at such Assembly proceed to elect and choose by Ballot, and they are hereby required to elect and choose, by a Majority of the Votes of the Members of the said Company then present, either in Person or by Proxy, Fifteen Persons, being Members of the said Company, to the Office of Directors of the said How to be Company; and in case no such Election of such Fifteen Directors shall be then made, then and in such Case another General Assembly of the said Company shall be holden on the following Monday for the Purpose of making such Election; and, from and after the Election of such Fifteen Persons as Directors, all the Powers and Authorities of the present Directors of the said Company shall cease and be null and void to all Intents and Purposes whatsoever.

And be it further enacted, That so often as the Office of Director shall become vacant by Death, Resignation, Disqualification, or Removal, the Survivors of such Directors, or the Majority of those remaining in Office, or any Five of more of them, shall and they are hereby required, within Thirty Days after such Vacancy shall happen, to call an Assembly of the said Company, in order to cleft a Person or Persons to be a Director or Directors in the Room or Stead of the Person or Persons who shall have died, resigned, become disqualified, or been removed; and the said Company, when so assembled, shall, and they are hereby required to elect a Person or Persons, qualified as aforesaid, in the Room or Stead of the Person or Persons who shall have died, resigned, become disqualified, or been removed as aforesaid; and such Person or Persons so elected shall continue in Office until the next annual Election of Directors of the said Company, and no longer, unless he or they shall be re-elected at such Election: Provided always, that no Person so chosen a Director of the said Company (except as herein is excepted) shall be capable of acting in the Execution of the said Office of Director, until he shall have taken the Oath for made the Affirmation being a Quaker) following; videlicet,

V. And be it further enacted, That it shall and may be lawful to and for the said Directors, or any Five or more of them, at all convenient Times and Places, to assemble for the Direction and Management of the Affairs of the said Company, and that such Directors, when so assembled, shall have full and exclusive Power to create and institute, or to abolish from Time to Time all such Offices under the said Company as they shall think it necessary or conducive to the Interest or well being thereof so to create, institute, or abolish; and they the said Directors shall also have full Power to annex to every Office under the said Company such Salary or Reward, or Salaries or Rewards, out of the Funds of the said Company, and to increase or diminish the Salary of any of the said Officers from Time to Time as they shall think proper; and they the said Directors are hereby authorized and empowered to appoint, suspend, or remove the Treasurer, and all Officers and Servants of the said Company; and that every Treasurer, Officer, and Servant of the said Company, when duly appointed, shall continue in such Situation until he shall be removed therefrom, without any new Appointment save as herein-after mentioned, and that the said Company shall in no Sort interfere with any of the said Matters; any Law, Custom, or Usage to the contrary in anywise notwithstanding.

VIII. And be it further enacted, That the said Directors, or any Five or more of them so assembled, shall and may exclusively direct and manage the Affairs of the said Company; and for the well ordering and managing thereof shall, in the Name of the said Company, have, enjoy, perform, and execute all the Powers, Authorities, and Privileges of the said Company, and do all Acts and Things in relation thereto, as fully and effectually, to all Intents and Purposes, as the said Company could or might have done previous to the passing of this Act, except as herein excepted or otherwise provided.

XV. XVII. GEORGII III. REGIS.

Cap. 24.

An Act for altering and enlarging the Powers of several Acts passed in the Thirty-first Year of the Reign of His late Majesty, and in the Tenth and Thirty-second Years of the Reign of His present Majesty, so far as relates to the Road from Leeds to Wakefield, in the County of York.

[7th April 1803.]

WHEREAS an Act was passed in the Thirty-first Year of the Reign of His late Majesty King George the Second, intituled, An Act for repairing the Road from Leeds to Sheffield, in the 31 County of York; whereby the said Road was divided into Two separate Districts, and a certain Division thereof as lies between the Towns of Leeds and Wakefield was directed to be within the First District of the said Road, and separate Tolls are authorized to be collected within each District, and directed to be applied towards repairing the said Road within the District wherein they are respectively collected: And whereas an Act IO was passed in the Tenth Year of His present Majesty's Reign, for enlarging the Term and Powers of the said Act, so far as relates to the said First District of the said Road: And whereas an Act was passed in the Thirty-second Year of the Reign of His said present Majesty, for enlarging the 3* Term and Powers of the said Act, so far as relates to the First District of Road: And whereas a considerable Sum of Money hath been borrowed, and is now due and owing upon the Credit of the Tolls authorized to be collected upon the Road within the said First District, which cannot be . And be it further enacted, That all Persons who shall hereafter advance Money or become entitled to any such Mortgages or Securities so to be made as aforesaid, shall (subject nevertheless to the Mortgages, Assignments, or Assurances, already made and exilling at the Time of the passing of this Act, and to the Payment of the several Sums of Money thereby secured), be Creditors on the Tolls hereby granted and imposed, or otherwise made payable, in equal Degree, in Proportion to the Sums of Money by them respectively advanced, or so secured as is herein-before directed, and shall not be entitled to any Preference by reason or on Pretence of the Priority of any Money being advanced.

VI. And be it further enacted, That the said Trustees may sue and be sued in the Name of their Clerk or Treasurer; and that no Action brought by or against the said Trustees, or any of them, by virtue or on account of this Act or the Acts herein-before mentioned, or any of them, in the Name of their Clerk or Treasurer, shall abate or be discontinued by the Death or Removal of such Clerk or Treasurer, or by the Act of such Clerk or Treasurer, without the Consent of the said Trustees; but the Clerk or Treasurer for the Time being to the said Trustees, may and shall, as often as it shall be thought necessary or adviseable, notwithstanding any want of Privity of Contraft, or otherwise howsoever, be made and deemed the Plaintiff or Defendant in such Action, as the Case shall be, so as that nevertheless nothing herein contained shall in anywise prevent or hinder the said Trustees, or any of them, or any Person or Persons for or on Behalf of them, or any of them, from suing, or protest them, or any of them, or any such Person or Persons, from being sued and proceeded against, in such Form of Action, and in such Manner, as it might or would have been lawful to do under or by virtue of the said Acts herein-before

IX. And whereas the Sum which by Law a Justice of the Peace is empowered to order for the Repairs of a Bridge suddenly injured by Floods has been found insufficient for such Purpose; be it therefore enacted by the Authority aforesaid, That, from and after passing of this Act, it shall and may be lawful to and for any Justice of the Peace for the County of Dublin, who shall be possessed of a Freehold Estate of the clear yearly Value of One hundred Pounds British, without Deductions, within the said County of Dublin, to nominate and appoint under his Hand and Seal an Overseer who can read and write, for the Purpose of repairing the Arch or Arches, Pier or Piers, or other Part or Parts of any Bridge within the said County that may be suddenly injured, damaged, or affected by any Flood or Torrent of Water, or other Accident; and such Overseer, when so nominated and appointed, shall have full Power and Authority to lay out and expend any Sum not exceeding Ten Pounds British, in repairing such Arch or Arches, Pier or Piers, or other Part or Parts of any such Bridge so injured, damaged, or affected, and the Charges and Expences thereof shall be accounted for and produced to, and allowed by the Grand Jury of the said County, in the Manner and Form directed by the said recited Act made in the Twenty-sixth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty.

X. And be it further enacted, That no Presentment for repairing any of the Roads in the County of Dublin aforesaid shall be granted, unless the fame be Twenty-one Feet wide between the Ditched, Drains, or Fences, unless where the fame is inclosed by Houses, or Lime and Stone Walls Four Feet high at the least; and that in every Place where a Presentment is applied for to widen any Road or Roads to the Breadth of Twenty-one Feet, the Gripe or Gripes shall be turned from the Road.

XI. And be it further enacted, That if any Horse, Mule, Afs, Bull, or Cow, Sheep, Goat, Pig, or other Beast, shall, at any Time after the passing of this Act, be found feeding or straying on any Road or Roads within the said County of Dublin, it shall and may be lawful to and for any Person or Persons whomsoever, to drive every such Horse, Mule, Afs, Bull, Ox, Cow, Sheep, Goat, Pig, or other Beast, to the next Pound, and there to detain every such Horse, Mule, Afs, Bull, Ox, Cow, Sheep, Goat, Pig, or other Beast, until the Owner or Owners of the same shall pay a Fine not exceeding Five Shillings IriJJ} Currency, for each and every Beast so impounded to the Person impounding the fame; and such Fine shall be levied and recovered in Manner directed by this Act.

XII. And be it farther enacted, That if any Person or Persons shall ride any Beast, or drive any Carriage, Carr, or Cart, on any Road within the said County of Dublin, save and except on the left Side of such Road, when meeting any Beast, Carriage, Carr, or Cart, every such Person so offending shall, for every such Offence, forfeit and pay any Sum not exceeding Ten Shillings Irish Currency; and such Penalty or Forfeiture shall be recovered on the Oath of One credible Witness, before any Justice of the Peace for the County of Dublin aforesaid, (which Oath such Justice is hereby; empowered to administer), or upon the View of such Justice of the Peace, and shall be levied by Warrant under the Hand and Seal of such Justice of the Peace, by Distress and Sale of the Horse, Beast, or Cattle, so ridden or driven on such Road, or of the Goods and Chattels of the Offender or Offenders, One Moiety whereof shall go to the Informer and the other Moiety to the Poor of the Parish wherein such Offence shall be committed; and the several Overseers of the several Roads in the said County of Dublin, shall and they are hereby required immediately after the passing of this Act, to put up and affix written or printed Notices in the most convenient Places on the said Road, specifying the Purport and Meaning of this Clause.

XIII. And whereas the Power of appointing a High Constable for each of the Baronies in the said County, (except the Baronies of Saint Sepulchres and Donore), and Four' Sub-Constables for each Barony in every Year, is vested in the Grand Jury of the said County at the General Quarter Sessions: And whereas it would be more proper to have the said High and Sub-Constables appointed by the Term Grand Jury of the said County; be it therefore enacted by the Authority aforesaid, That the Term Grand Jury of the said County shall every Year, at Easter Term, appoint a proper Person to be High Constable for’each of the Baronies in the said County of Dublin, (except the Baronies of Saint Sepulchres and Donore), and shall also appoint Four proper Persons to be Sub-Constables for each of such Baronies, (except the said Baronies of Saint Sepulchres and Donore'), to preserve the Peace at the Quarter Sessions and Elections, and at all Times and Places in the said County: Provided always, that every such High Constable shall have the like Powers and Authorities, and be subject to the like Pains and Penalties as if he had been appointed by the Grand Jury at the Easter Quarter Sessions; and that no Sum or Sums of Money shall be paid to any such Sub-Constable for his Trouble in executing the said Office, by the Treasurer of the said County, unless such Sub-Constable shall produce to the said Treasurer a Certificate signed by the Clerk of the Peace of the said County, that he had at some Quarter Sessions or Adjournment thereof for the said County, since his Appointment to such Office, duly qualified himself agreeable to an Act, passed in the Second Year of Her late Majesty Queen Anne, intituled, An Act to prevent the further Growth of Popery.

and thence through the Town and Parish of South Petherton, in the said County, unto and through the several Parishes of Shepton, Beauchamp, and Barrington, in the said County, to the Turnpike Road leading from Ilminster to Langport, in the said County; GEORGII III. REGIS.

Cap. 28.

An Act for continuing the Term, and altering and enlarging the Powers of Two Acts, passed in the Thirty-third Year of the Reign of His late Majesty, and the Twenty-first Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for amending, widening, and keeping in Repair the Roads from 'Tamworth to Ashby-de-la- Zouch in the County of Leicester, and from Sawley Ferry, now Harrington Bridge, in the said County, to a Turnpike Gate at or near the End of Swar cliffe La?ie to Ashby-de-la-Zouch aforesaid.

[7th April 1803.]

WHEREAS an Act was passed in the Thirty-third Year of the Reign of His late Majesty King George the Second, intituled, An Act for amending, uidening, and keeping in Repair the High Roads from the Borough of Tamworth to Alhbv-de-la-Zouch in the County of Leicester, and from Sawley Ferry in the said County, to a Turnpike Gate at or near the End of Swarcliffe Lane leading to Aftibv-de-la-Zouch aforesaid: And whereas another Act was passed in the Twenty-first Year of His present Majesty to enlarge the Term and Powers of the said Act: And whereas the Trustees named in and appointed by and by virtue of the said recited Acts have proceeded to put the fame in Execution, and have borrowed several considerable Sums of Money on the Credit of the Tolls authorized and directed to be taken by the said recited Acts, which, together with the Tolls colltfted, have been applied in amending and [Loc. id Per.2 - 6 A repaying

XVII. XVIII. And be it further enacted, That the said Trustees may sue and be sued for or concerning any Thing done by virtue and in pursuance of this Act, in the Name of their Treasurer for the Time being; and that no Action or Suit, to be brought or commenced by the Direction of or against the said Trustees by virtue of this Act in the Name of their Treasurer, shall abate or be discontinued by the Death or Removal of any such Treasurer, nor by the Act of such Treasurer, without the Consent of the said Trustees, or any Five or more of them, at a Meeting holden in pursuance of this Act, but that the Treasurer for the Time being to the said Trustees shall be deemed to be the Plaintiff or Defendant, as the Case may be, in every such Action: Provided always, that every such Treasurer, in whose Name any Action or Suit shall be commenced, prosecuted, or defended in pursuance of this Act, shall be fully indemnified, reimbursed, and paid out of the Monies to arise by virtue of this Act, all such Colls, Charges, Damages, and Expences, as by the Event, or in cohsequence of any such Action or Proceeding, he shall pay, bear, expend, or be put unto or become chargeable with by Reason of his being so made Plaintiff or Defendant as aforesaid.

Annoyance, or Inconvenience of Persons travelling thereon, every Person so offending shall, for every such Offence, forfeit and pay any Sum not exceeding Forty Shillings nor less than Ten Shillings.

V. And whereas Difpures may arise touching the Boundaries of the said Parish of Garrijlown, be it therefore enabled. That the said Commissioners shall, and they are hereby required, to perambulate the Boundaries of the said Parish of Garrijlown, and to cause Notice of such ii.tended Perambulation to be inserted in the said Dublin Journal, or Dublin Evening Post, if then published, and if not, then in some other Newspaper printed and circulated within the said County of Dublin, Ten Days at lead before the Time of such intended Perambulation; and after the Expiration of the Time to be specified in such Notice, they the said Commissioners are hereby authorized and required to enquire into, let out and ascertain, fix and determine the Boundaries of the said Parish of Garrijlown, and within Thirty Days after the Determination of the said Boundaries, to cause a Description of such Boundaries to be inferred in the said Dublin Jour-rial, or Dublin Evening Post, if then published, and if not, then in some other Newspaper printed and circulated within the said County of Dublin.

VI. Provided always, That if any Person or Persons interested in the Determination of the said Commissioners respecting the said Boundaries shall be dissatisfied with such Determination, such Person or Persons may appeal to the Justices of the Peace acting in and for the said County of Dublin, at any Quarter Session of the Peace to be holden within Four Calendar Months next after the Publication as aforesaid of the Description of the said Boundaries (the Party or Parties making such Appeal giving Ten Days Notice of such Appeal, and of the Matter thereof, to the said Commissioners, or any Two of them); and the Decision of the said Justices therein shall be final and conclusive.

VII. And whereas it may shorten the Boundary Fences between the Lands lying in the said Parish of Garrijlown, and the Lands lying in the Parish or Parishes adjoining thereto, if the said Commissioners were empowered to cause such Fences to be raised in such Directions as they shall think most proper and convenient for shortening and making the same regular; be it therefore enacted, That it shall and may be lawful to and for the said Commissioners, with the Consent in Writing under the Hand or Hands of the major Part in Value of the Land Owners in any Parish or Parillies adjoining to the said Parish of Garrijlown, and also under the Hand or Hands of the Lord or Lords, Lady or Ladies, of the Manor or Manors in any such adjoining Parish or Parities, or of the Owner or Owners of the Land upon which such Fence or Fences shall or may be intended to be made, to set out, ascertain, and determine the Boundary Fences to be made between the Lands and Grounds lying in the said Parish of Garrif-town, and the Lands lying in such adjoining Parish or Parishes, as they shall judge proper for the Purposes aforesaid; and after such Boundaries shall be Tet out, ascertained, and determined as aforesaid, the same shall be fenced in such Manner, and at such Time or Times, as the said Commissioners shall direct; and shall fur ever thereafter be deemed and taken to be the Boundaries between the said Parish of Garrijlown and such adjoining Parish or Parishes, any Law, Usage, or Custom to the contrary thereof notwithstanding.

And be it further enacted, That no Person shall be subject or liable to pay more than Two Tolls in any One Day, to be computed from Twelve of the Clock in One Night to Twelve of the Clock in the succeeding Night, for palTing and repassing with the fame Horses, Cattle, Beads, or Carriages, through all or any Gate or Turnpike Gates or Turnpikes to be erected by virtue of this Act; but that all and every Person and Persons having paid the said Two Tolls in the Whole, and such Person producing a Ticket denoting that the respective Toll hath been paid on that Day (which Ticket the Collectors of the Tolls are hereby required to deliver grads'), shall pass and repass the same Day with the fame Horses, Cattle, Beads and Carriages Toll-free, through all the Turnpikes or Toll Gates to be erected on the said Road by virtue of this Act.

XVII. And be it further enacted, That if any Person or Persons shall, with any Cattle or Carriage, pass through any Land, Ground, or Place (not being a publick Highway) adjoining to or lying near any of the said Roads; or if any Owner or Occupier of any such Land, Ground, or Place, shall knowingly or wilfully permit or suffer any Person or Persons, with any Cattle or Carriage whatsoever, to pass through the fame, whereby the Payment of any of the said Tolls shall be evaded; or if any Person or Persons shall give to or receive from any Person or Persons, other than the Person or Persons appointed to collect the said Tolls, any Note or Ticket by this Act directed to be given by the Collectors of the said Tolls, or shall forge or counterfeit any such Note or Ticket, or make use of any such forged or counterfeited Note or Ticket, knowing the same to have been forged or counterfeited, whereby the Payment of the said Tolls, or any Part thereof, shall be evaded; or if any Person or Persons shall forcibly pass through any of the said Turnpikes with any Horse, Carriage, or other Cattle, without Payment of the Tolls for the fame, or shall take off or cause to be taken off any Horse, or other Cattle, from any Carriage; or shall leave or cause to be left upon or near any Part of the said Roads, any Carriage, Horse, or other Cattle, or any Goods, or shall do any other Act in order or with Intent to evade the Payment of the said Tolls, or any Part thereof, every Person so offending in any of the Cases aforesaid shall for every such Offence forfeit the Sum of Forty Shilling,s One Moiety whereof shall be paid to the Informer or Informers, and the other Moiety shall be applied towards the Purposes of this Act.

GEORGII III. REGIS.

V

Cap. 32.

An Act to amend and render more effectual an Act made in the Twentieth Year of the Reign of His late Majesty, for repairing, improving, and maintaining, the Public Conduits and other Waterworks belonging to the Town of Southampton.

[17th May 1803.]

WHEREAS an Act was passed in the Twentieth Year of the Reign of His late Majesty King George the Second, intituled An Act for repairing, improving, and maintaining the Public Conduits and Aff'zoGee 2. other Waterworks belonging to the Town of Southampton: And whereas the Powers and Provisions of the said Act and the Money raised under the fame have, by Experience, been found wholly inadequate and insufficient for the Purposes intended by the said Act; and it is therefore become necessary for the more effectually supplying the said Town with Water, that the said Act Should be amended, and further and other Powers and Provisions granted and made for the Purpose of securing to the Inhabitants of the said Town and Shipping resorting to the Port of the said Town, a more abundant Supply of Water; and also for the more effectual Prevention and extinguishing of Fires, and providing Fire Engines and Fire Men within the said Town; and that the Money necessary for the Purposes aforesaid should be raised by an equal and more adequate Assessment: May it therefore please your Majesty, That ir may be enacted; and be it enacted by the King’s Most Excellent Majesty, by and with the Advice and Consent of the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and Commons, in this present Parliament assembled, and by the Authority Appoint-of the fame, That from and after the Second Wednesday after passing this ment and Act so much of the said recited Act as relates to the Appointment, Election of

534 43° GEORGII III. Cap. 32.

Qualification, Election, and Meetings of the Commissioners of Waterworks within the said Town, and to the Nomination and Appointment of Treasurer, Clerk, Assessors, and other Officers; and also as to the making, raising, levying, and collecting, any Rate or Assessment for the Purposes of the said Act shall be, and the fame is hereby repealed.

XXI. And whereas it may happen that many Persons liable to, and who may be rated and assessed for the Purposes of this Act, may, before the Payment of the Sum which may be rated on them respectively, quit and leave their Grounds, Dwelling-Houses, Shops, Ware-Houses, Coach-Houses, Stables, Cellars, Vaults, Buildings, or Tenements, and remove out of the Limits aforesaid, and thereby endeavour to avoid the Payment of the said Rates and Assessments; be it therefore enacted, That when any Person or Persons who hath or have been so rated and assessed, shall quit his or their Ground, House, Shop, Ware-House, Coach-House, Stable, Cellar, Vault, Building, or Tenement, before he, she, or they shall have paid the said Rate or Assessment, and shall afterwards refusetopay the lame when due and demanded by the Collector or Collectors authorized and appointed to receive the same, that then and in every such Case it shall and may be lawful to and for the said Collector or Collectors, or One of them, by Warrant according to the Form or Effect in the Schedule hereunto annexed, under the Hands and Seals of Two of His Majesty's Justices of the Peace for the said Town and County, which Warrant the said Justices are hereby authorised and required to grant; and such Warrant being first backed or countersigned, by some Magistrate of the County, City, or Liberty where the Distress is to be made, which Warrant such Magistrate is hereby required to back or counter-sign, to distrain the Goods and Chattels of such Person or Persons so refusing or neglecting, and to sell the same, rendering the Overplus (if any be), after having deducted the reasonable Charges and Expences of such Distress and Sale, to the Owner or Owners of such Goods and Chattels respectively, upon Demand thereof made.

XXII. And whereas there are divers Houses and Tenements within the said Town which are let at small Rents, or are let out in Lodgings or separate Apartments, or ready furnished, by which Means the Payment of the Rate or Assessment for such Houses and Tenements may be evaded; for remedy whereof be it enacted, That where any House or Tenement, or any Part thereof, shall be let cut in Lodgings or separate Apartments, or ready furnished, the Landlord or Landlords, Owner or Owners thereof, shall be deemed and taken to be the Occupier or Occupiers of, and shall be rated to and pay the Rates of Assessments in respect of such Houses or Tenements.

Cap. 33.

An Act for enabling the Most Noble John Duke of Atholl and his Heirs to build a Bridge over the River Tay, at or near to the Town of Dunkeld in the County of Perth, and make Roads of Communication thereunto. [T^th May 1803.]

WHEREAS the Two Ferries upon the River Tay, at or near the Town of Dunkeld, in the County of Perth, called the Ferry of Invar, and the Lower or East Ferry, are often liable to great Interruptions, and the Passage across the said River is sometimes attended with considerable Danger, owing to the Rapidity of the said River, whereby the Communication between the Northern and Southern Pans of Great Britain is much impeded: And whereas the Roads leading to the same are unlafe and inconvenient: And whereas the Most Noble John Duke of Atholl is the foie Proprietor of the said Ferries, and of the Land adjoining thereto on both Sides of the said River: And whereas the said John Duke of Atholl is willing and desirous to give up to the Public the Tolls and Duties derived from those Ferries, and to build a Bridge over the said River at or near to the said d own of , Dunkeld, and to make good and convenient Roads to communicate therewith, whereby great Advantage will accrue to the Public: But lauleful and expensive an Undertaking cannot be executed without the Authority of Parliament: May it therein Lee. And be it further enacted, That if any Person or Persons shall haul or draw, or cause to be hauled or drawn, upon any Part of the said Bridge, or upon any of the said Roads, any Tree or Piece of Timber, or any Stone or other Thing whatsoever, otherwise than upon Wheel Carriages, or shall suffer any Tree or Piece of Timber, or any Stone or any other Thing whatsoever, which shall be conveyed upon Wheel Carriages, to drag upon any Part of the said Bridge or Roads, every Person or Persons so acting shall for every such Offence forfeit and pay any Sum not exceeding Twenty Shillings Sterling.

And be it enacted, That the Right and Property of the said Veiling the Bridge so to be built or repaired, with the Toll-House and Turnpike- Bridge in the Gate to be built and erected, and the Materials thereof, are hereby Duke and vetted in the said Duke and his Heirs; and he or they is and are hereby hls Heirs-empowered to bring, or cause to be brought, Actions in his or their

Name or Names against any Person or Persons who shall damage the fame, or disturb him or them in the Possession thereof.

XXVIII. And be it further enacted, That in case the said Bridge shall Ferry to be at any Time or Times be so far out of Repair, or be in such Condition provided in that the Passage over the same shall be dangerous, or be prevented, B^ideelhmild it shall be lawful for the said Duke or his Heirs, and he or they is become inland are hereby required, during the Period that any Tolls or Pontage passable. Duties shall be paid for patting over the said Bridge, as often

as Occasion shall require, to provide One or more proper and convenient Ferry Boat or Boats for the PafTige of Persons, Lattle, and Carriages across the said River Tay, at such Place or Places as he or they shall judge to be most proper or convenient, and as near to the said Bridge as conveniently may be, and to take for Passage over the said River by such Boat or Boats, such Tolls or Duties as are hereby directed to be paid for patting over the said Bridge; and shall and may tile the fame Methods for Recovery thereof as are herein prescribed for recovering the Toll or Pontage Duty for Passage over the said bridge.

XXIX. And be it further enacted, That all the Powers hereby granted shall commence on the Third Tuesday after the passing of this present Act.

XXX. And be it further enacted, That all Penalties and Forfeitures by this Act inflicted or authorised to be imposed in relation to the said Bridge, Tolls, or Pontage Duties, or in any Matter or Thing of and concerning the same, the Manner of recovering and levying whereof is not otherwise particularly directed, shall, upon Proof of the said Offence, before any Two or more Justices of the Peace of the said County of Perth, either by the Confession of the Party or other legal Evidence, be levied by Distress and Sale of the Goods and Chattels of the Party or Parties so offending, by Warrant under the Hands of such Justices, (which Warrant such Justices are hereby authorised and required to grant for those Purposes, and also to administer Oaths gratis,) such Sale being always made by Public Roup of Auction to the highest Bidder, at such Place as shall be directed by the said Warrant, within Five Days after such Distress shall have been made, and the Overplus Money arising from such Sale (after such Penakies are recovered, and the Charges of levying and recovering the same are deduced,) shall be returned on Demand to the Owner or Owners of such Goods and Chattels, and all Penalties and Forfeitures, if not otherwise directed to be applied by virtue of this Act, shall, from Time to Time during the Continuance of the said Tolls, be paid to the said Duke or his Heirs, and after the Cessation thereof to the Treasurer of the said County, and shall be laid out and applied for the Purposes of this Act, and in case sufficient Distress cannot be found, or such Penalties or Forfeitures shall not forthwith be paid, it shall be lawful for any Two or more of the said Justices, and they are hereby authorised and required to cause such Offender or Offenders to be committed to the House of Correction or Common Gaol of the said County, there to remain for any Time not exceeding Three Calendar Months, unless such Penalties and Forfeitures and all reasonable Charges shall be sooner paid and satisfied.

XXXI. Provided always, and be it further enacted, That all Actions for all and every the Penalties by this Act imposed shall be commenced within Six Calendar Months after the Fast from which the Penalty arises was committed, and not afterwards.

XXXII. And be it enacted, That if any Person or Persons shall think him, her, or themselves aggrieved by any Order or other Proceeding of the said Duke or his Heirs, or by any Order of One or more Justice or Justices of the Peace not assembled in Quarter Sessions, it shall and may be lawful for him, her, or them, to appeal to the Justices of the Peace for the said County of Perth at their next General Quarter Sessions assembled, who are hereby authorized and empowered to hear and determine the Matter in Dispute, and whole Order thereon shall be final and conclusive without further Appeal.

XXXIII. And be it further enacted, That this Act shall bedeemedaPub-lic Act, and be judicially taken Notice of as such by all Judges, Justices, and other Persons whomsoever, without specially pleading the same.

And be it enacted.That it shall not be lawful for any Tacksman of the Tolls, or Toll-gatherer, or other Person employed to collect any of the Tolls or Duties, to take or receive, directly or indirectly, any Idler or other Tolls and Duties than what are appointed to be levied and exacted by this and the before-recited Acts, unless where a General Meeting of Trustees shall have authorized any of the Tolls and Duties to be lessened; or to fell Ale, Spirits, or Articles of any Kind within any of the Toll-houses, or in any other House, or at any Place within a Quarter of a Mile of any Turnpike-gate, unless in so far as he shall be expressly authorized so to do, by Warrant of a General Meeting of Trustees, or to absent himfdf from the Turnpike-gate, so as to occasion Delay or Inconvenience to Travellers; or to refuse, when required by any Person passing through the Turnpike Gate, to shew his Warrant of Collection; and every Person offending in any of the Particulars aforesaid, shall for every such Offence forfeit and pay a Fine not under Ten Shillings nor exceeding Forty Shillings besides full Costs of Suit.

XLI. And be it enacted, That it shall not be lawful for any Cliaife Driver to fit in his Chaise, or for any Carter or the Driver of any other Carriage of the like Kind to ride upon his Cart or other Carriage, while passing through the Streets of any City, Town, or Village in the said County, or upon any Highway within the Toll Bars next adjoining to the said City oi Edinburgh; and every Chaise Driver fitting in his Chaise beyond the above Limits shall resume his proper Station, and every Carter riding upon his Cart or Carriage beyond the said Limits shall dismount, when either of them shall be thereto required by any Person, apprehending Danger; provided always that nothing herein contained shall extend to any Coach, Chaise, Phaeton, Curricle, Chair, or other Carriage usually driven by a Person fitting within or upon the Carriage; neither shall it be lawful for any Person to take Charge of more than Two Single Horse Carts, or of more than One other Carriage, or for the Driver of any Waggon, Wain, Cart, Coach, Chaise, or other Carriage, or of any Horse, Afs, Mule, or other Bead of Draught, to drive or permit the same to travel or pass upon any Part of the Roads within the County of Edinburgh, abreast or alongside of any other Waggon, Wain, Cart, Coach, Chaise, or other Carriage, or of any Horie, Afs, Mule, or other Bead of Draught, but all such Carts and Carriages and Beasts of Draught above described, going in the fame Di-redtion, shall drive in a Line, with a Bridle or Halter affixed to the Head of each Horse or other Bead of Draught, and in the Hand of the Driver j and all such Drivers upon meeting any other Waggon, Wain, Cart, Coach, Chaile, or other Carriage, loaded or unloaded, or any Person travelling on Horseback or with a loaded Horse, shall give way by

XLII. And be it enacted, That in all Cases under this Act or the before-recited Acts, where no Provision is made to the contrary, any Person offending may, without any Warrant or Peace Officer, be apprehended by the Person injured or intending to inform or prosecute, with such Aid as he can procure, and be by him or them carried before the next Justice of the Peace, who is hereby required to deal with such Offender as is herein-before dirrded; and the Horses, Carts, or Carriages of such Offender may be seized and detained till the Penalties shall be paid; and in all other Cases any Person or Persons whatever, knowing of any Offence committed against this Act, may lodge Information thereof with the Procurator Fiscal of the County of Edinburgh, who is hereby required, as he shall be answerable, to prefer a Summary Complaint to any One or more Justice or Justices of the Peace of the said County, or to the Sheriff Depute or Substitute thereof; and either the said Justice or Justices, or the Sheriff Depute or Substitute, may thereupon proceed against the Offender or Offenders in a summary Way, but with Liberty never-thelels to any Person conceiving himself to be aggrieved by the Sentence of such Justice or Justices, to appeal to the next General Quarter Sessions of the Peace, but not afterwards; and in all Cases the said Justice or Justices, and the Sheriff Depute or Substitute, may convict upon the Confession of the Offender, or on the Oath of One or more credible Witness or Witnesses -, and in case the Fine be not in-stantly paid, the Offender may be committed to any Jail, or to the Bridewell or House of Correction, till Payment, or failing thereof, until the Expiration of any Time not exceeding Two Calendar Months from the Day of Commitment, or the Goods and Chattels of the Offender may be distrained and sold by Warrant of the said Justice or Justices, or of the Sheriff Depute or his Substitute, for Payment of the Sums awarded, and the Persons so distraining are hereby authorized to fell the Goods or Chattels so distrained, and to return the Overplus to the Owner, after the reasonable Charges of distraining, keeping, and felling have been first deducted.

Cap. 35.

An Adfc for making and maintaining a Railway from or from near a Place called Pitlake Meadow, in the Town of Croydon, to or near to the Town of Reigate, in the County of Surrey, with aCollateral Branch from the said Railway, at or near a Place called Merjlham, in the Parish of Merjlham, to or near to a Place called Godstone Green, in the Parish of Godstone, all in the said County of Surrey.

[17th May 1803.]

WHEREAS the making and maintaining a Railway for the Passage of Waggons and other Carriages, from or from near a Place called Piilake Meadow in the Town of Croydon, in the Parish of Croydon, in the County of Surrey, to or near to a Place called Reigate, in the Parish of Reigate, in the said County; and also a Collateral Branch from the said Railway, at or near a Place called Merjlham, in the Parish of Mers.ham, to or near to a Place called Godstone Green, in the Parish of Godstone, all in the said County of Surrey, will be of very great Advantage to several considerable Manufactories established in the Neighbourhood, and to the Inhabitants of many Towns and Places, and of a very populous Country lying on or near to the Line of the said intended Railway, by opening a cheap and easy Communication for the [Loc. & Per.] ‘ 7 L Conveyance

VII. And be it further enacted, That the Lands and Grounds to be taken or uled for the making and tiling of the said Railway shall not exceed Sixty Yards in Breadth, exetpt in such Places where it shall be judged necessary for Waggons or other Carriages to turn, lie, or pass each other; orwheieany Warehouses, Cranes, or Weigh Beams may be erected; or where any Places may be fee out or appropriated for the Reception or Delivery of Goods, Wares, and Merchandize, which shall be conveyed on the said Railway, and not above Eighty Yards in Breadth in any Place, without the Conicnt of the Owners of the Lands or Hereditaments adjoining to the said Railway.

VIII. Whereas it having been found necessary for the better conducing of the said Railway, that it should pass through a small Part of the Parish and Estate of Gatton, as is described or delineated by the Plan, to be at or near Mr. Avery's Farm at Batik Bridge, and the Owr.er of the said Parish and Estate, being desirous to give every Facility to the said Undertaking; be it therefore enacted, That the said Railway, shall pass over that Part of the Estate and Parish of Gatton so described, gratuitously and without any Rent or Recompence whatever for such Permission, so long as the present Railway Corporation, or Company shall continue, cr that the said Railway shall continue to be used as a Railway, but for no other Purpose whatever.

IX. And be it also enacted, That the Owner of the said Parish and Estate shall continue to be assessed to, and to pay all Parliamentary or Parochial Taxes, Rates, and Assessments for and in respeift of the Land occupied by the said Railway, the said Land continuing to be in every respect Part of the Estate of Gatton, as if this Right of Railway had never been granted.

X. And be it further enacted, That the Breadth of such Railway shall not exceed Twenty-four Feet, excepting what may be required for a Base of an Embankment so far as it may extend, and at the Expence of the Railway Company, be fenced off with a strong close Oak Paling Six Feet in Height with a Gate at each End, to be kept in good Condition and Repair by the said Railway Company; the Key of such Gates to be kept by the Owner of the Gatton Estate, who, for the Purpose of afierting or keeping up his Rights, shall be infilled One Hour in every Year to lock such Gates: Also that no Buildings of any Description shall ever be erected upon or over the Land of the Gpttcn Estate by the said Railway Company across which the present Right of Railway is meant to be granted, nor over or upon any other Part of the said Estate without the express Granc or Permission of the Owner of the said Estate, in Writing under his Hand and Seal first had and obtained.

XI. And be it further enacted, That if at any Time hereafter the said Railway shall be dilufed, or by Neglect or other Means be rendered or become impassable for a Period of Two Years, in such Case the Owner of the Parish and Estate of Gatton, shall be and is hereby empowered to resume the Right of Railway now granted, and to rC.possess and to occupy the Land meantto be fetoff and allotted for a Railway, in the full.ft Manner as if the present Act had never passed or been carried into Effect.

And, in Consideration of the great Charge and Expence which the said Company mult incur and sustain in making and maintaining the said Railway, and other Works hereby authorized to be made and maintained, be it further enacted, That it shall be lawful for the said Company from Time to Time, and at all Times hereaftir, to alk, demand, take, recover, and receive, to and for the Ufeand Benefit of the said Company, for the Tonnage and Wharfage of all Goods, Wares, and Merchandize, and other Things, which shall be carried or conveyed upon any Part of the said Railway, such Rates and Duties as the said Company shall think fit, not exceeding the Rates herein-afeer mentioned; (that is to say).

For all Dung, Two-pence per Ton per Mile:

For all Limestone, Chalk, Lime, and all other Manure (except Dung), Clay, Breeze, Allies, Sand, and Bricks, Three-pence per Ton per Mile:

For all Timber, Tin, Copper, Lead, Iron, Stone, Flint.', Coals, Charcoal, Coke, Culm, Fullers Earth, Corn and Seeds, Hour, Malt, and Potatoes, Four-pence per Ton per Mile:

And for all other Goods, Wares, and Merchandize, and Things whatsoever. Sixpence per Ton per Mile:

And in all Cases where there shall be a Fraction of a Ton, a Proportion of the said Rates Brail be demanded and taken for such Fraction, according to the Number of Quarters of a Ton contained in such Fraflion; and where there shall be a Fraction of a Quarter of a Ton, such Fraction shall be deemed and considered as a whole Quarter of a Ton; and in all Cases where there shaft be a Fradlion of a Mile in the Distance which any Waggon or other Carriage shall pass upon the said Railway, such Fraction shall, in ascertaining the said Rates, be deemed and considered as a Mile: And in order to ascertain such Distances, the said Company shall cause the said Railway to be

And be it further enacted, That no Action, Suit, or Information, shall be brought, commenced, or prosecuted, against any Person or Persons, for any Thing done in pursuance of this Act, or in Execution of any of the Powers or Authorities, or any of the Orders made, given, or directed, in, by, or under this Act, unless One Calendar Month’s previous Notice, in Writing, shall be given by the Person or Persons intending to commence and prosecute such Action, Suit, or Information, to the said Company, or to their Clerk or Treasurer for the Time being, nor unless such Action, Suit, or Information, shall be brought or commenced within Three Calendar Months next after the Fact committed, for which such Action, Suit, or Information, shall be so brought, commenced, or prosecuted; Cap. 37.

An A<fl for paving, cleaning, lighting, watching, and improving the Borough of King sLynn^ in the County of Norfolk; and for removing Nuisances and Annoyances therein; and for holding the Saturday and Bead; Markets within more convenient Parts of the said Borough.

[17th May 1803.]

WHEREAS the Street*, Lanes, publick Passages, and Ways, within the Borough of King's Lynn, in the County of Norfolk, are not properly paved, cleansed, lighted, or watched, and are subject to various Nuisances, Annoyances, and Encroachments, and many of such Streets, Lanes, Passages, and Ways, are narrow and incommodious: And whereas it would tend greatly to the Benefit, Convenience, and Safety of the Inhabitants of the said Borough, and of all Persons retorting thereto, if the said Streets, Lanes, publick Passages, and Ways, were properly paved, cleansed, lighted, and watched, and if all Nuisances, Annoyances, and Encroachments therein, were removed, and if Provision were made for preventing the like in future, and if a new and commodious Road or Carriage Way were made from the South Gates of the Borough aforesaid, into a Street called Saint James's Street, in the Parish of Saint Margaret, within the said Borough: And whereas the Provisions contained in an Act made in the Twelfth and Thirteenth Years £Loc. & Per.2 8 D of

Cap. 38.

VI. And be it further enacted, That np Person who shall have or enjoy any Place of Profit arising out of or by reason of the respective Tolls hereby granted, shall be capable of ailing as a Trullee during his Enjoyment of such Place of Profit, nor shall any Trustee be capable of acting in any Case wherein he shall be personally interested, otherwise than as a Creditor on the respective Tolls hereby granted and made payable: Provided nevertheless, that such Trustees as are or shall be Justices of the Peace shall and may, in their respective Jurisdictions, act as Justices of the Peace in the Execution of this Act, notwithstanding their being Trustees, except only in such Cases where they shall be personally interested.

VII. And be it further enacted, That when and so often as any Trustee or Trustees shall die or refuse to act, it shall be lawful for the surviving or remaining Trustees for each of the said Districts respectively, by Writing under their Hands, from Time to Time, to elect and appoint One other Person to be a Trustee in the room or Head of each Trustee so dying or refusing to act; but Notice of the Time and Place of the Meeting for every such Election of a new Trustee or Trustees shall be given by the Clerk for the Time being to the said respective Trustees, by affixing a Copy of such Notice on each of the Gates or Turnpikes which Hull be then erected in the said respective Districts, at least Fourteen Days before every such Meeting; and every such Person who shall from Tune to Time be so elected and appointed as aforesaid, shall be and he is hereby veiled with the fame Powers for putting this Act in Execution in the said respective Districts for which he shall be so elected and appointed, as if such Person had been named in and appointed by this Act.

VIII. And be it further enacted, That the said respective Trustees acting in the Execution of this Act, shall and may sue and be surd in the Name of their respective Clerks; and that no Action which shall be commenced, (ued, prosecuted, or defended, by or against the said mpec-tive Trustees, or any of them, by virtue or on Account of this Act, in the Name of their respective Clerks as aforesaid, shall abate or be discontinued by the Death or Removal of such Clerks, or by the Act or Default of such Clerks, without the Consent of the respective Trustees, at a Meeting to be holden in pursuance of this Act; but the Clerk to the said respective Trustees for the Time being shall be deemed Plaintiff or Defendant in every such Action, as the Case may be: Provided always, that each such Clerk, in whose Name any Action or Suit shall be commenced, prosecuted, or defended, in pursuance of this Act, shall be re-imburled and paid out of the Monies to be raised by virtue of this Act, all such Costs, Damages, and Charges, as by the Event of every such Proceeding he shall be put to or become chargeable with, by Occasion of his being lo made Plaintiff or Defendant.

Upon any Emergency, be thought necessary by the said respective Trustees that an earlier Day of Meeting should be appointed than that Day to which the last Meeting shall have been adjourned, the Clerk to the said respective Trustees, by an Order in Writing signed by any Two or more of such respective Trustees, (although not assembled at a Meeting), appointing the Time, Place, and Purpose of such earlier Meeting, shall forthwi h give Notice of such earlier Meeting in the Manner before directed, such Time not being less than Ten Days after such Notice; and all Proceedings of the said respective Trustees, at such Meetings to be appointed as last mentioned, shall be as valid as they would have been in case the respective Trustees had met in pursuance of an Adjournment.

XII. And be it further enacted, That all the Orders and Proceedings of the said respective Trustees in the Execution of this Act, and the Names of the Trustees present at each respective Meeting, shall be entered in Books to be kept by their respective Clerk for that Purpose, and signed by the respective Chairman and Clerk present at each Meeting, or either of them; and that every such Book shall be open at all seasonable Times to the Inspection of any of the said respective Trustees, or of the Creditors on the respective Tolls hereby granted and made payable, who shall be at Liberty to have and take Copies thereof or Extracts therefrom, paying for every such Copy or Extract the Sum of Sixpence for every Seventy-two Words, and so in Proportion for any greater or less Number of Words; which said Entries duly signed as aforesaid shall be deemed Originals, and shall be read and admitted as Evidence in Cases of Appeal, and in all Suits or Actions in any Court whatsoever touching any Thing done or to be done in pursuance of this Act.

XL. And be it further enacted, That if any Owner or Occupier of any Lands adjoining to any Part of the said Road, or near to any of the said Turnpikes, shall knowingly permit or suffer any Person or Persons to pals through or over any part of their said Lands, or through any Gate, Passage, Inclosure, or private Way, with any Horse, Cattle, or Carriage; or if any Person or Persons shall pass through or over any such Lands, Gate, Passage, Inclosure, or private Way, with any Horse, Cattle, or Carriage or if any Person or Persons shall take o(f or cause to be taken off from any Carriage any Horse or other Bead, or any Part of the Loading of any such Carriage, in order to lessen or reduce its Weight, with Intent to evade the Payment of the said respective Tolls, or whereby the Payment of any of the said respective Tolls or any Part thereof respectively shall or may be avoided, every Person so offending in any of the Cases aforesaid, shall for every such Offence forfeit and pay any Sum not exceeding Five Pounds nor less than Thirty Shillings.

and if any such Parish or Township Surveyor or Surveyors shall neglect or refuse to do as he and they is and are hereby required and directed to do, or shall wilfully return incorrect or imperfect Lifts, he and they shall respectively forfeit and pay the Sum of Five Pounds for every such Refusal or Neglect; and if any Person or Persons keeping a Team or Teams, Draught or Draughts, Cart or Carts, Wain or Wains, and chargeable towards repairing the said Road, shall, after such Summons or Notice as aforesaid, neglect or refuse to fend their respective Teams, Draughts, Carts, or Wains, furnished with Labourers, Oxen, or Horses, according to the Custom of the Country, and proper Tools to do and perform such their respective Days Works upon the said Road, he, she, or they so neglecting or refusing, shall forfeit and pay the Sum of Ten Shillings for every Day that each Team, Draught, Cart, or Wain shall be wanting, or #iall not be duly employed in that Service; and if any Person or Persons who shall be sent with any Team, Draught, Cart, or Wain to work on the said Road, shall be found idle or negligent, it shall be deemed as if such Team, Wain, Draught, or Cart had not been lent to work on the said Road, and the same Sum shall be accordingly forfeited and paid; and if any Statute Work shall not be performed within the Year in which the fame is due, the same shall be performed in the Course of the succeeding Year.

LXXII. And be it further enacted, That the said respective Trustees shall cause the said Road in their said respective Districts to be measured, and Stones or Posts to be set up in or near the Sides of the said Road, at the Distance of One Mile from each other, denoting the Distance of every such Stone or Poll from any Town or Place, as the said respective Trustees shall think proper, and also proper Direction Posts; and if any Person shall wilfully pull up or damage any of such Posts or Stones, or shall obliterate or deface any of the Letters, Figures, or Marks which shall be inscribed thereon, and be thereof convicted before any Two or more Justice or Justices of the Peace for the said respective Counties, either by Confession of the Party or by the Oath of One or more credible Witness or Witnesses, every such Person so offending shall forfeit and pay any Sum not exceeding Five Pounds nor less than Twenty Shillings for each Stone or Poll, Letter, Figure, or Mark so wilfully broken, pulled up, obliterated, or defaced, to be levied and recovered as herein-after mentioned; or if any Person shall ride upon any Footway adjoining to any Part of the said Road, or shall wilfully or carelessly drive any Horse or other Bead or Cattle, or any Swine, or any Cart or Carriage thereon, or shall cause any Damage to be done to any of such Footways; or if any Driver of any Waggon or other Carriage shall wilfully or carelessly break or damage any of the Posts or Stones erected for the Security of the said Footways, or drive the Wheel of his Carriage against the fame, or the Side or Sides of the said Footways; or if any Person shall hale or draw, or cause to be haled or drawn upon any Part of the said Roads any Tree or Piece of Timber, or any Stone, otherwise than upon Wheel Carriages, or shall suffer any Part of any Tree or Piece of Timber which shall be conveyed upon any Wheel Carriage to drag upon any Part of the said Road, or shall plough over or drag any Plough upon any Part of the said Road, or in ploughing shall turn any Horse or other Beast drawing any such Plough upon any Part of the said Road to the Prejudice thereof, or if any Person or Persons shall lay any Hay, Straw, or other Matter or Thing upon any Part of the said Road, to be made into Manure, or shall ferape off the fame, or any Mud, Soil, or other Matter or Thing which shall be or lie upon any Part of the said Road with any sharp pointed Instruments, so as to damage the said Road or any Part thereof; or if any Person or Persons shall leave any Waggon, Wain, Cart, or other Carriage in, upon, or on the Sides of the said Road, either with or without any Horse or Beast harnessed or yoked thereto, or shall lay any Piece of Timber, or any Stones, Brick, Hay, Straw, Lime, Dung, Manure, Soil, Rubbish, or other Matter or Thing whatsoever in any Part of the said Roads, or on the Side or Sides thereof to the Prejudice thereof, or to the Annoyance of any Person or Persons travelling thereon, and be convicted thereof respectively, by the Confession of the Party, or by the Oath of One or more credible Witness or Witnesses, before any One or more Justice or Justices of the Peace for the said respective Counties, every Person so offending shall forfeit and pay a Sum not less than Ten Shillings nor more than Forty Shillings for every such Offence, One Moiety whereof shall be allowed and paid to the Informer, and the other Moiety shall be applied to the Purposes of this Act within the said respective Districts.

LXXIV. LXXV. And whereas Persons guilty of Offences against this Act may be transient Persons, unknown to the Collectors, Surveyors, or other Officers under this Act; be it therefore further enacted, That it shall be lawful for any of the said Collectors, Surveyors, or other Officers respectively, to seize and detain any such unknown Person or Persons guilty of any Offence as aforesaid, and to convey him, her, or them before One or more Justice or Justices of the Peace for the County or Place where any such Offence or Offences shall be committed without any other Warrant or Authority than this Act for so doing; and such Justice or Justices of the Peace respectively is and are hereby empowered and directed to proceed immediately to the Conviction or Acquittal of such Offender or Offenders, or to oblige such Person or Persons so offending to give Security for his, her, or their Appearance at the next Petty or Special Sessions to be holden for the County or Place where such Offence or Offences shall be committed, and on such Conviction, or for Want of sufficient Security, to commie the Person or Persons so offending to the Common Gaol or House of Correction for the County, District, or Place where the Offence shall be committed, there to remain until he, (lie, or they shall pay the respective Penalty by him, her, or them incurred for such Offence or Offences, or shall give such Security as aforesaid.

Cap. 41.

An A<H for enabling the High Court of Chancery to authorize and empower the surviving Deviseein Trust named in the Will of ‘Thomas Batty, heretofore of the Parish of Saint George in the East, in the County of Middlesex, Gentleman, deceased, to grant Building Leases of certain Ground at or ntax Church Lane, in the Parish of Saint George in the East, in the County of Middlesex, devised to him by the fame Will; and to fell and pull down an ancient Messuage Handing on Part of the said Ground, and to apply the Monies to arise by such Sale upon the Trusts of the said Will.

[17th May 1803.]

WHEREAS Thomas Batty, heretofore of the Parish of Saint George in the East, in the County of Middlesex, Gentleman, having been at the Time of making and publishing his last Will and Testament, and thence to the Time of his Decease, seised for an Estate in Fee Simple of and in and well entitled in his own Right to a Messuage or Tenement, and a certain Piece of Ground formerly called Piper's Close, but since converted into and now or lately used as Garden Ground, containing Four Acres Two Roods and Twenty-four Poles, formerly in the Parish of Stepney alias Stebunheath, but now of Saint George in the East, in the County of Middlesex aforesaid fsubjett only to a Lease thereof made by the said Thomas Batty unto Charles Berner, of Church Lane, in the Parish of Saint Mary, Whitechapel, in the County of Middlesex, Gardener, bearer. 1st Per.'} 9 M ing

Will of Thomas Batty,

ing Date the Nineteenth Day of July One thousand seven hundred and eighty-three, for a Term of Forty-one Years, from Michaelmas One thousand seven hundred and eighty three, at the Rent of Twenty ^ounds per Annum, reserved to the said Thomas Batty, his Heirs and Assigns, with a Covenant on the Part of the said Thomas Batty to renew such Lease for a further Term of Twenty-one Years), did in and by his said last Will and Testament in Writing, bearing Date the Twenty-second Day of April One thousand seven hundred and eighty-five, and executed in such Manner as the Statute prescribes for rendering valid the Devises of Freehold Estates, give and devise the fame Messuage and Ground unto Isaac Ellis, of White he pel, in the said County of Middlesex, Wheelwright, and unto John Flexney, late of South End, in the County of Kent, Farmer, since dead, and their Heirs, to the Use of them and their Heirs during the natural Life of his (the Testator’s) Niece, Mary Jones (then the Wife of William Jones since deceased) but now the Wife of the said Charles Berner (the Lessee aforesaid) upon Trust, to pay the Rents, I (hues, and Profits thereof into the proper Hands of his (the Deflator's) said Niece, or to such Person or Persons as (he should by any Writing under her Hand direct or appoint, for the Term of her Life, to and for her foie and separate Use and Benefit, exclusively of the said William Jones her Husband, or any Husband ihe might thenafter happen to marry; and the said Testator did by his said Will declare that the fame should not be subject or liable to the Debts, Controul, or Engagements, of the said William Jones, or of any future Husband in anywise, and that the Receipt or Receipts of the said Mary Jones, signed by her alone, should from Time ±0 Time notwithstanding her Coverture, or any future Coverture, be a good and sufficient Discharge, and good and sufficient Discharges to the said Isaac Ellis and John Flexney, their Heirs, Executors, and Administrators, for such Rents, Issues, and Profits, or so much thereof as should be therein acknowledged or expressed to be received; and from and immediately after the Decease of the said Mary Jones, the said Testator did by his said Will declare, that the said Messuage or Tenement and Ground should be divided into Two equal Parts or Shares, the One Half of which should be considered as divided into as many Shares as there should be Children of the said Mary Jones, who should be living at the Time of her Decease, or dead having left any Child or Children who should be living at the Time of the Decease of the said Mary Jones; and the said Testator did thereby declare that each of the Children of the said Mary Jones, who should be living at the Time of her Decease, should have and be entitled to One of such Shares; and that the Child and Children of every of them who should have died leaving any Child or Children who should be living at the Time of the Death of the said Mary Jones should have and be entitled to another of the said Shares; and that if there should happen to be Two or more who should be entitled to any such Share or Shares, or Parts or Divisions thereof, they should take the same as Tenants in Common and not as Joint Tenants; and that all and every such Child or Children should be entitled to such Shares and the Parts and Divisions thereof to them and their respective Heirs for ever $ and the said Testator did by his said Will give and devise the said Moiety of the said Gardens, House, and Ground, from and immediately after the Decease of the said Mary Jones, to such her Child and Children, Grand Child and Grand Children, and their Heirs for ever, according to such their respective Shares and Interests therein; and in case there should be only One such Child or Grand Child who should be

An Act for dividing, allotting, and inclosing the Open and Common Fields, Ings, Meadows, Stinted Pastures, Moors, Commons, Wastes, and other uninclosed Lands and Grounds within the Township of Stowe, and the Hamlets of Sturton and Branjby, in the Parish of Stowe, in the County of Lincoln.

[17th May 1803.]

and the Verdict or Verdicts which shall be given in such Action or Actions shall be final, binding, and conclusive, upon all and every Person and Persons whomsoever, unless the Court wherein such Action or Actions shall be brought shall set aside such Verdict, and order a new Trial to be had thereon, which it shall be lawful for the Court to do as is usual in other Cases; Cap. 43.

An Act for dividing, allotting, and inclosing the several Commons and Waste Grounds within the Manor of Norton, in the Parishes of Norton and Dronfield, in the County of Derby.

[17th May 1803.]

WHEREAS there are within the Manor and Parish of Norton, in the County of Derby, certain Commons or Parcels of Waste Ground, containing together by Estimation One hundred and forty Acres or thereabouts, upon which the Owners or Proprietors of Houses, Lands, Tenements, and Hereditaments, within the said Manor and Parish, are in Right thereof entitled to Common of Pasture for all their Commonable Cattle levant and couchant upon their said respective Tenements: And whereas there are within the said Manor of Norton, in the Parish of Dronfield, in the said County of Derby, certain ether Commons or Parcels of Waste Ground, containing together by Estimation One hundred and thirty Acres or thereabouts, upon which the Owners or Proprietors of Houses, Lands, Tenements, and Hereditaments, within the said Manor of Norton, and Parish of Dronfield, are in Right thereof entitled to Common of Pasture for all their Commonable Cattle levant and couchanc upon their said respective Tenements: And whereas Samuel Shore the Lord of the younger, Esquire, is Lord of the Manor of Norton aforesaid, and as such Manor‘ is Owner of the Soil of the said several Commons and Waste Grounds: And whereas Peter Robinson Clerk, is Vicar and Lecturer of Norton aforesaid, and as such is entitled to certain Glebe Lands within the said Manor, and \L*c. iff Per.~\ 9 T to
