V. And whereas Accidents do happen, and Mischiefs are frequently done by Persons driving Carts and other Carriages on the said Roads, for Remedy whereof in future, be it enacted, That if the Driver or any other Person or Persons having the Care of any Cart, Car, Dray, Wain, or Waggon, shall by Negligence or wilful Misbehaviour cause any Hurt, Damage, or Injury to any Person or Persons, or to any Coach, Cart, or other Carriage travelling on the said Roads, or shall quit the said Roads, and go on the other Side of the Hedge or Fence inclosing the said Roads, or wilfully be at such a Distance from such Cart, Car, Dray, Wain, or Waggon, or in such a Situation (whilst the same shall be passing on the said Roads) that he or they cannot have the Direction, Care, and Management of the Horses drawing the fame, or shall by Negligence or wilful Misbehaviour prevent, hinder, or interrupt the free Passage of any other Carriage whatever, or of any of His Majesty's Subjects; or if the Driver of any empty or unloaded Cart, Car, Dray, Wain, or Waggon, shall refuse or neglect to turn aside and make way for any Coach, Chariot, Chaise, loaded Waggon, Cart, or other loaded Carriage; or if any Person shall drive or aft as the Driver of any such Coach, Chaise, Poftchaife, or other Carriage let for Hire, or any Waggon, Wain, or Cart, not having the Name or Names of the Owner or Owners thereof painted thereon as by Law required, or shall cover over and conceal such Name or Names from being seen and read, or shall refuse to discover the reaj and true Christain and Surname, and Place or Places of Abode of the Owner or Owners of such Carts or other Carriages, every Person or Persons so offending in any of the Cases aforesaid, and being lawfully convicted of any such Offence, shall forfeit and pay any Sum of Money not exceeding Forty Shillings, in case such Driver be not the Owner of such Cart or other Carriage; and in case the Offender or Offenders be the Owner or Owners of such Cart or other Carriage, then any Sum not exceeding Five Pounds, and in case of Non-payment of such Penalties upon Demand, such Person or Persons shall be committed to the Common Gaol or House of Correction for the said respective Counties, for any Time not exceeding Two Calendar Months, there to remain until such Penalty shall be sooner paid and satisfied j and the Driver of any such Carts or other Carriages in any or either of the said Cases, shall and may by Authority of this or the said recited Act, with or without any other Warrant or Authority than this Act, be apprehended by any Person or Persons who (half fee such Offence committed, and shall be immediately conveyed and delivered over to a Constable or other Peace Officer, in order to be conveyed before some Justice of the Peace for the said respective Counties, to be dealt with according to Law; and if any such Driver, in any of the said Cases, shall refuse to discover his Name and Place of Abode, it shall be lawful for the Justice before whom he shall be taken, or to whom any such Complaint shall be made, to commit such Driver to the Common Gaol or House of Correction for the said respective Counties, there to remain for any Time not exceeding Three Calendar Months, or otherwise to proceed against him for such Penalty as aforesaid in such Manner as such Justice shall think proper, for the Recovery thereof; and the Owner or Owners of such Cart, Car, Dray, Wain, Waggbn, or other Carriage shall be answerable for such Penalty or Penalties incurred and forfeited by the Driver or Drivers thereof.

And be it further enacted, That the said Trustees may sue and be sued in the Name of their Clerk or Treasurer; and that no Action to be brought or commenced by or against the said Trustees, by virtue or on Account of the said first herein-before recited Act, or of this Act, in the Name of their Clerk or Treasurer, shall abate or be discontinued by the Death or Removal of such Clerk or Treasurer, or by the Act of such Clerk or Treasurer, without the Consent of the said Trustees, but the Clerk or Treasurer for the Time being respectively to the said Trustees shall always be deemed the Plaintiff or Defendant, in such Action (as the Case shall be): Provided always, that such Trustees, and every such Clerk or Treasurer in whose Name any such Action shall be commenced, sued, prosecuteti, or defended in pursuance of the said first herein-before recited Act and this Act, shall always be reimbursed and paid out of any Money to arise by virtue of the said Act and this Act, all such Colts, Charges, Damages, and Expences, as by the Event, or in consequence of any such Proceedings they or he shall respectively be put unto, or become chargeable with, by reason of his being so made Plaintiff or Defendant as aforesaid.

X. Provided also, and be it further enacted, That where such Money so agreed or awarded to be paid as next before mentioned, shall be less than Twenty Pounds, then and in all such Cases the same shall be applied to the Use of the Person or Persons who would for the Time being have been entitled to the Rents and Profits of the Lands, Grounds, or Hereditaments so purchased, taken, or used for the Purposes of the said Act and this Act, in such Manner as the said Trustees shall think fit; or in case of Infancy or Lunacy, then to his, her, or their Guardian or Guardians, Committee or Committees, to and for the Use and Benefit of such Person or Persons so entitled respectively.

ANNO QUADRAGESIMO TERTIO

GEORGII III. REGIS.

Cap. 67.

An Act for amending, widening, altering, and improving the Road leading from the High Street in the Town of Arundel, to the Junction of the Pet-worth and Pulborough Roads, and from thence to join the present Turnpike Road on Fittleworth Common, in the County of Sussex.

[nth June 1803.]

WHEREAS the Road leading from the High Street in the Town of Arundel, in the County of Sussex, through the several Parities of Arundel, Houghton, and Bury to the Junction of the Petworth and Pulborough Roads in the Parish of Bury, and from thence towards the Town of Petworth to the Turnpike Road on Fittleworth Common, is in a ruinous State and Condition, and in many Parts narrow and incommodious for Travellers and Carriages, and cannot be effectually amended, widened, altered, and improved by the ordinary Course of Law: May it therefore please Your Majesty that it may be enacted; and be it enacted by the King’s most Excellent Majesty, by and with the Advice and Consent of the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and Commons, in this present Parliament assembled, and by the Authority of the same, That Lord George Henry Lenox, Sir Cecil, Bifshopp Baronet, Sir George Trustees Thomas Baronet, Sir George P cknell Knight, the Mayor of Arundel for the Time being, Charles Alcock Clerk, Thomas Bushby, Robert Bushby,

Qualification

II. Provided always, and be it further enacted, That no Person shall ot Trustees. be capable of acting as a Trustee in the Execution of this Act, unless he shall be in his own Right, or in the Right of his Wife, in the actual Possession and Enjoyment or Receipt of the Rents and Profits of Messuages, Lands, Tenements, or other Hereditaments of the clear yearly Value of Fifty Pounds, or shall be Heir Apparent of some Person having such an Estate of the clear yearly Value of One hundred Pounds, or be possessed of a Personal Estate to the Amount of One thousand Pounds; and if any Person not being so qualified shall nevertheless act as a Trustee in the Execution of this Act, every such Person shall for every such Offence forfeit and pay the Sum of Fifty Pounds to any Person or Persons who shall sue for the same, to be recovered in any of His Majesty's Courts of Record at Westminster, by Action of Debt or on the Cafe, or by Bill, Suit, or Information; and every Person so prosecuted shall prove that he is qualified, or otherwise shall pay the said Penalty upon Proof given of his having acted as a Trustee in the Execution of this Act; Provided nevertheless, that all Acts and Proceedings which shall have been done and performed by any such Person touching the Execution of this Act previous to his being convicted of the Offence before mentioned, shall, notwithstanding such Conviction, be as valid and effectual as if such Trustte: may Person had been qualified according to the Directions of this Act: Pro-act as justces. vided always, that such of the said Trustees as are or shall be in the Commission of the Peace for the County of Sussex, may nevertheless act as Justices of the Peace in the Execution of this Act, except only in such Cases where they shall be personally interested; but no Person shall be capable of acting as a Trustee in the Execution of this Act in any Case

For every Horse, Mare, Gelding, Mule, or Afs, laden or unladen, and not drawing, the Sum of One Penny:

For every Drove of Oxen, Cows, or other Neat Cattle, the Sum of Ten-pence per Score, and so in Proportion for any lesser Number:

Cap. 68.

An Act for continuing the Term and altering and enlarging the Powers of Two Acts, passed in the First and Twenty-third Years of the Reign of His present Majesty, for making a Road from the North East Side of the Goswell Street Road, next Islington, and near to the Road called The New Road over the Fields to Old Street, and from the Dog House Bar to the End of Chiswell Street, by the Artillery Ground, in the County of Middlesex.

[nth June 1803.]

An Act for making, widening, and repairing a Road from the North East Side of the Goswell Street Road, next Islington, in the County of Middlesex, and near to the Road called The New Road, over the Fields and Grounds to Old Street Road, opposite to the Dog House Bar, and at [Loc. & Per.J 14 H and

which Money (fill remains due, and cannot be repaid, nor can the said Road be properly maintained and improved, unless the Term of the said Acts is further continued, and some of the Powers and Provisions thereof altered, amended, and enlarged: May it therefore please Y ur Majesty that it may be enacted; and be it enacted by the King’s most Excellent Majesty, by and with the Advice and Consent of the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and Commons, in this present Parliament assembled, and by the Authority of the same, That the said recited Acts, passed in the First and Twenty-third Years of the Reign of His present Majesty, and all and every the Tolls, Powers, Authorities, Provisions, Regulations, Penalties, Forfeitures, Clauses, Matters, and Things whatsoever therein contained (except such as relate to Exemptions from Stamp Duties, or as are hereby varied, altered, or repealed), shall be and the same are hereby further continued for and during the Term herein-after mentioned, as fully and effectually, to all Intents and Purposes, if the fame were repeated and re-enacted in the Body of this Act; but subject nevertheless to the Amendments, Alterations, Variations, and Additions herein contained; and which shall commence and take Efteft imine iately upon the passing of this Act; and this Act, and the additional Term hereby granted, shall be subject and liable to the Payment of all Money now due and owing on the Credit or on Account of the said recited Acts, or which may hereafter be borrowed on the Credit of the said recited Acts and this Act, and the Interest due and to grow due thereon respectively.

And whereas by virtue of several Acts now in force for collecting a Toll (commonly called A Sunday Toll), on the several Roads leading out of the Metropolis, certain Persons are from Time to Time appointed and have Authority to collect such Tolls at the Toll Gate erected by virtue of the said recited Acts, and great Inconvenience frequency arises from the Names of such Persons not being known to Persons liable to pay the said Tolls; be it therefore enacted, That all Persons hereafter appointed to collect such Sunday Tolls as aforesaid, at the said Toll Gate or Gates erected or to be erected on the said Road by virtue of the said recited Acts or this Act, shall cause their Christian and Surnames, with the Words " SUNDAY TOLL," to be painted on a Board on a Black Ground in White Letters, of not less than Three Inches in Length, and of a proportionate Breadth, and shall cause such Board to be hung up in some conspicuous Place on the Front of the Toll House or Toll Gate at which the said Collector or Collectors shall attend to collect the said Tolls; and if any Person shall demand Payment of or shall receive any such Toll without having such Board hung up as aforesaid, or shall refuse upon Demand to tell his or her real Name and Place of Abode, he or (Ire shall for every such Offence forfeit and pay any Sum not exceeding Forty Shillings.

IV. And whereas it is by the said first recited Act provided and di-reded, that no Part of the said Road shall be paved; which Restriction, from the Increase of Houses and Buildings in the Neighbourhood of some Part of the said Road, and the great Wear of some Parts thereof, hath been found inconvenient; be it therefore further enacted, That so much of the said first; recited Act as restrains the said Trustees from paving any Part of the said Road, shall be and the fame is hereby repealed; and that it shall be lawful for the said Trustees, or any Five or more of them, from Time to Time to cause such Part or Parts of the said Road to be paved as they shall deem necessary and expedient for the better Accommodation of the Publick, and such Pavement to be repaired from Time to Time in such Manner as they shall think proper; and to defray the Expence of such paving and repairing of the Pavement from Time to Time by and out of the Monies collected or to be collected upon the said Road by virtue of the said recited Acts and this Act.

VI. And whereas the said Road is greatly frequented by Foot Passengers as well as by Carriages and Persons on Horseback, and the Practice of Stable Keepers, Horse Dealers, and other Persons exercising and breaking in Hori'es in Carriages and otherwise, is of late become a great Nui-fance, and frequently endangers the Lives of His Majesty's Subjects passing and repassing upon the said Road; for Remedy whereof, be it further enacted, I hat if any Person or Persons shall exercise or drive any Horse, Mare, or Gelding in any Carriage upon the said Road, in Manner and for the Purpose above mentioned, every such Person so offending, or the Stable Keeper, Horse Dealer, or Stable Keepers, under whose Care and Controul the said Horses and Carriages shall then be, shall forfeit and pay for every Offence any Sum not exceeding Forty Shillings; or if any Person or Persons shall run or drive any Wheel or Wheelbarrow or Sledge upon any Part of the Footpath belonging to the said Road, or set or place, or cause to be set or placed thereon, or upon any Part of the said Road or Footpath any Stall, Shewboard, Calk, Package, Timber, Stones, Bricks, Lime, or any other Thing whatsoever, so as to obstru£t the free Passage of the said Road or Footpaths, he, she, or they shall, for every such Offence, forfeit any Sum not exceeding Ten Shillings; which said Penalties or Forfeitures shall be recoveted before any One of His Majesty's Justices of the Peace for the said County, and shall also be applied in like Manner as any other Penalty or Forfeiture is in and by the said first recited Act directed to be recovered and applied.

VII. And be it further enacted, That it shall be lawful for any Person or Persons, without any Warrant or other Authority than this Act, to apprehend any Offender or Offenders in the Premises against this Act, and with all convenient Speed to convey and deliver him, her, or them, to the Constable or other Peace Officer nearest to be found to the Place where the Offence shall have been committed, who is hereby authorized and required to take Rich Offender into Custody, in order to his, her, or their being taken or conveyed before a Magistrate to be dealt with according to Law.

And be it further enacted, That if any Horse, Cattle, or other Beast, upon which any Toll is by this Act imposed, or any Waggon, Wain, Cart, or other Carriage,' shall pass through any Turnpike or Toll Gate to be erected by virtue of this Act, Five Times or more in any One Day, to be computed from Twelve of the Clock at Night to Twelve of the Clock in the next succeeding Night, every such Horse, Cattle, or other Beast, and every such Waggon, Wain, Cart, or other C arriage, shall be subject and liable to pay Double the respective lolls herein-before granted, which said respective Sums of Money shall be demanded and taken in the Name of or as Toll; and if any Person or Persons subject to the Payment of any of the said Tolls, shall, after Demand thereof made, neglect or refuse to pay the fame or any Part thereof, it shall be lawful for the Person or Persons appointed as aforesaid for collecting such Tolls, to seize and d stram any Horse, Bead, or other Cattle, or any of their Harness or Accoutrements; and if such Tolls, and the reasonable Charges of such Seizure and Distress, shall not be paid within the Space of Four Days after such Distress made, the Person or Persons so distraining shall and may fell the Horse, Cattle, Beast, or Thing' so distrained, returning the Overplus, (if any there be , upon Demand, to the Owner thereof, after such Tolls, and all reasonable Charges of making such Distress and Sale, shall be deduded; and that all Tolls collected and levied by virtue of this Act upon the said Ruad, shall be and the same are hereby vested in the said Trustees, and shall be applied and disposed of in such Manner as is herein after mentioned.

XIV. And, to obviate any Doubts which may arise with respect to such Four-wheeled Carriages as consist of Two Wheels of the Breadth of Six Inches, and Two of a less Breadth, be it further enacted, That all such Carriages with Four Wheels, Two whereof shall be of a less Breadth than Six Inches, although the other Two shall be of a greater Breadth, which shall pass through any Gate or Turnpike erected or to be erected upon the said Road, shall be liable to and charged with the Tolls and Duties by this Act imposed upon every Waggon, Wain, or other Four-wheeled Carriage, having the Fellies of the Wheels of less Breadth than Six Inches.

XVII. And be it further enacted, That if any Person or Persons shall with any Horse, Cattle, or Carriage whatsoever, pass through any Land, Ground, or Hereditaments, belonging to any Person or Persons whomsoever, or through or over any Common or Wade Ground adjoining to or lying near any Turnpike or Toll Gate to be erected by virtue of this Act, (the fame not being a publick Highway or ancient private Road), or if any Owner or Occupier of such Land, Ground, or Hereditaments, shall knowingly permit or suffer any Person or Persons with any Horse, Cattle, or Carriage whatsoever, to pass through the fame, whereby the Payment of the said Tolls, or any Part thereof, shall be avoided; or if any Person or Persons shall take off, or cause to be taken off, any Horse or Cattle from any such Carriage, or shall leave or cause to be left upon or near to any Part of the said Road, any Horse, Cattle, or Carriage, with an Intent to avoid paying any of the said Tolls, or any Part thereof; or if any Person or Persons shall forcibly pals through any such Turnpike or Toll Gate with any Horse, or other Cattle or Bead, without Payment of Toll; or if any Person shall forge or counterfeit, or offer to dispol'e of any Note or Ticket denoting the Payment of Toll, to any other Person whomsoever, in order to evade the Payment of the said Tolls; or if any Person shall receive or make Use of the fame with that Intent, or shall do any other Act with an Intent to evade Payment of Toil, or whereby such Payment shall be evaded, every Person lo offending, in each and every of the Cases aforesaid, shall for every such Offence respectively forfeit and pay any Sum not exceeding Forty Shillings, One Moiety whereof shall be paid to the Informer or Informers, and the other Moiety shall be applied in such Manner as other Penalties are by this Act directed to be applied.

XX. Provided also, and be it further enacted, That no Toll shall be demanded or taken at any Side Gate or Turnpike on the Line of the said Road for any Horse or other Beall, or Cattle, which shall only cross the said Road, and which shall not go or travel or be driven thereon exceeding the Distance of One hundred Yards.

XXI. And be it further enacted, That in case any Dispute, Suit, or Litigation shall arise touching or in anywise relating to the said Tolls, or the Recovery thereof, the Person or Persons appointed to collect the fame, or any other Person or Persons acting by or under the Authority of the said Trustees, shall be and are hereby declared to be competent to give Evidence in any such Dispute, Suit, or Litigation.

XXII. Provided always, and be it further enacted, That it shall not be lawful for the said Trustees, during the Continuance of this Act, to set up or erect, or cause to be set up or erected any Turnpike Gate or Toll Bar in, upon, across, or on the Side or Sides of such Part of the said intended Road as lies between a Lane called Halton Lane, and another Lane called Hellifield Lane, both in the Township of Hellifield, in the County of York, or within One hundred Yards of each of the said Lands.

XXIII. And be it further enacted, That the Right and Property of all the Turnpikes or Toll Gates, Bars, Rails and Fences, Toll Houses, and Buildings, to be erected or provided by virtue of this Act, and the Right and Property of the Materials to be provided for erecting, building, or repairing the fame, or any of them respectively, and also of all the Tools, Materials, and other Requisites got, provided, orcollefted for any of the Purposes of this Act, shall be and are hereby vested in the said Trustees, and they, or any Seven or more of them, are hereby empowered to dispose thereof as they shall think proper, for the Purposes of this Act, and bring or cause to be brought any A^ioq or Aftaons, or to prefer or order the preferring of any Indictment or Indictments against any Person or Persons who shall take, Heal, carry away, break down, injure, or spoil the fame, or any Part thereof, or disturb the Trustees, their Agents, or Servants, in the Possession thereof.

XLV. Provided also, and be it further enacted, That where such Money so agreed or awarded to be paid as next before mentioned, shall be less than Twenty Pounds, then and in all such Cases the same shall be applied to the Use of the Person or Persons who would for the Time being have been entitled to the Rents and Profits of the Hereditaments so purchased, taken, or used for the Purpose of this Act, as the said Trustees, or any Seven or more of them shall think fit, or in case of Infancy or Lunacy, then to his, her, or their Guardian or Guardians, Committee or Committees, to and for the Use and Benefit of such Person or Persons so entitled respectively.

IV. Provided always and be it further enacted, That the Purchaser or Purchasers of all or any Part of the Manors, Towns, Lands, and Premises by this Act limited to be sold, paying his or their Purchase-Money to them the said Trustees or the Survivor of them, or the Heirs of such Survivor, shall be acquitted and discharged of and from the same, and not be obliged to fee or look to the Disposal or Application thereof.

Cap. 76.

An Act for repealing an Act, passed in the Seventh Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for dividing and inclosing the Open Commons in the Manor of Reagill, in the County of Westmorland; and for granting other Powers for dividing, allotting, and inclosing the said Lands and Grounds.

[nth June 1803.]

WHEREAS an Act was passed in the Seventh Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, An Act for dividing and inclojing the Open Commons, in the Manor of Reagill, in the County of Westmorland, whereby it was amongst other Things enabled, that the said Wastes and Commons lying and being within the said Manor of Reagill, should, on or before the Twentieth Day of May One thousand seven hundred and sixty-seven, or as soon after as conveniently [Loc. & Per.] 15 X could

One Month next after such Death or Refusal, by Writing under their Hands and Seals, elect a Commissioner, not interested in the said intended Inclosure, in the Stead and Place of every Commissioner dying or refuting to act as aforesaid: And whereas no Division or Allotment was made, nor any other Act done under or by virtue of the said in Part recited Act: And whereas the Commissioners thereby appointed have since departed this Life, without appointing any other Commissioner or Commissioners pursuant to the said Power, whereby it is now become difficult or impossible to carry the Provisions of the said Act into Effect: And whereas there are within the Manor of Reagill, in the County of Westmorland, several Open Commons, Moors, and Waste Grounds, containing Six hundred Acres or thereabouts: And whereas the Right Honourable William Lord Lowther Baron of Whitehaven, in the County of Cumberland, is Lord of the Manor and Owner of the Soil of the said Commons, Moors, and Waste Grounds, and of the Coal Mines, Veins, and Seams of Coal, and all other Mines and Minerals therein: And whereas it would be a very great Advantage to the several Owners and Proprietors of and Persons interested in the said Commons, Moors, and Waste Grounds, if the fame were divided and inclosed, and specifick Parts thereof divided and allotted unto and Amongst the several Persons interested therein, according to their respective Rights, Shares, and Interests: And whereas an Act was passed in the Forty-first Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, An Act for consolidating in One Ail certain Provisions usually inserted in Acts of Inclosure; and for facilitating the Mode of proving the several Fails usually required on the passing of such Acts: And whereas it is requisite that greater Powers flioold be given for that Purpose than those contained In the said recited Act, and therefore and on Account of the Death of the said Commissioners, it is expedient that the same Act should be repealed; but such Repeal, Division, Allotment, and Inclosure, cannot be effected without the Aid and Authority of Parliament: May it therefore please Your Majesty that it may be enacted; and be it enacted by the King’s most Excellent Majesty, by and with the Advice and Consent of the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and Commons, in this present Parliament assembled, and by the Authority of the same, That the said in Part recited Act, passed in the Seventh Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, and every Matter, Clause, and Thing therein contained, shall be and the fame is and are hereby repealed.

ANNO QUADRAGESIMO TERTIO

GEORGII III. REGIS.

An A<fl for repealing an Act, passed in the Nineteenth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, An Act for dividing and inclosing the Open Wafies and Commons lying in the Manor of Sleagill, in the County of Westmorland; and for granting other Powers for dividing, allotting, and inclohng the said Lands and Grounds. [nth June 1803.]

WHEREAS an Act was passed in the Nineteenth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, An Act for dividing and inclosing the Open Wajles and Commons lying in the Manor of Sleagill, in the County of Westmorland, whereby it was amongst other Things enacted, that the said Wastes and Commons lying and being within the said Manor of Sleagill, should, on or before the Twentieth Day of September One thousand seven hundred and seventy-nine, or as soon after as conveniently could be done, be divided, set out, and allotted, by John Moore Esquire, George Wheatley, and Thomas Gibson, Commissioners appointed by the said Act, and their Successors, or any Two or more of them, in the Manner and subject to the Rules, Orders, and Directions therein-after mentioned: And it was thereby further enacted, that when and so often as any One of the Commissioners appointed by the said Act, or to be elected in Manner therein-after mentioned, should die, or refuse to act, the surviving Commissioners, or any Two or more of them, should from Time to Time, within Two Months next after such Death or Refusal, by Writing under their Hands and Seals, elect a Commissioner, not interested in the said intended Inclosure, in the Stead and Place of every Commissioner dying or refilling to act as aforesaid: And whereas

and for facilitating the Mode of proving the several Fids usually required on the passing of such Acts: And whereas it is requisite that greater Powers should be given for that Purpose than those contained in the said recited Act, and therefore and on Account of the Death of the said Commissioners, it is expedient that the same Act should be repealed; but such Repeal, Division, Allotment, and Inclosure, cannot be effected without the Aid and Authority of Parliament: May it therefore please Your Majesty that it may be enacted; and be it enacted by the King’s most Excellent Majesty, by and with the Advice and Consent of the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and Commons, in this present Parliament assembled, and by the Authority of the same, That the said in Part recited Act, passed in the Nineteenth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, and every Matter, Clause, and Thing therein contained, shall be and the fame is and are hereby repealed.

II. And be it further enacted, That James Wilson of Kendal in the said County of Westmorland Esquire, the surviving Commissioner nominated and appointed under and by virtue of the Provisions in the said recited Act, passed in the Nineteenth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, and John Gibson of Oddendale, Esquire, shall be and they are hereby appointed the Commissioners for dividing, allotting, and inclosing the said Commons, Moors, and Waste Grounds, pursuant to the Directions and Provisions of this Act, and also pursuant to the Directions and Provisions of the said last recited Act, passed in the Forty-first Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, except where the same are by this Act varied or altered.

And be it further enacted, That nothing in this Act contained shall extend, or be deemed or taken to revoke, make void, alter, or annul any Settlement, Deed, Will, or Limitation, or to prejudice any Person having or claiming any Jointure, Dower, Portion, Reversion, Rent, Service, Debt, Charge, or Incumbrance, of, in, out of, upon, or affecting any of the Lands and Grounds so intended to be divided and inclosed, or which shall be exchanged in pursuance of this Act, or any Part thereof respectively; but that the several Lands and Grounds to be assigned and allotted upon such Division and inclosure to the several Parties concerned, or their Trustees, and which shall be taken in Exchange in pursuance of this Act, shall, immediately after such Alltoments or Exchanges shall be made, be, remain, and enure, and the several Persons to whom the same shall be allotted and assigned, or given in Exchange as aforesaid, shall from thenceforth stand and be seised thereof, to and for such and the same Uses and Estates, and subject to such and the fame Wills, Settlements, Limitations, Remainders, Charges, Tenures, Rents, Services, C^uit Rents, and Incumbrances, as the said several Lands, Grounds, Tenements, or Hereditaments, in lieu or in respect whereof such Allotments and Exchanges shall be made as aforesaid, now are, or should or would have been subject and liable to be charged with or affected by, in case the fame had remained uninclosed and unexchanged, or this Act had not been parted.

Cap. 79;

An Act for dividing, allotting, and inclosing the Open and Common Fields, and Common Pasture, Common and Walle Lands, within the Township of Middleton, in the Parish of Middleton, in the East Riding of the County of York.

[nth June 1803.]

WHEREAS within the Township of Middleton, in the Parish of Middleton in the East Riding of the County of York, there are several Open Fields called the Little East Field, Swung Close Field, Sand Pit Field, Middle West Field, Mill Field, and Bainton Gate Field, which contain together Two thousand Acres or thereabouts; and there is also a certain Common Pasture called the Horse Wold, Cow Wold, and Sheep Wold, which contains Onethoufandeight hundred Acres or thereabouts; and there are also certain ancient Lanes or Common or Waste Lands, which contain Two Acres or thereabouts: And whereas the Most Noble William Duke of Devonshire is Lord of the Manor of Middleton aforesaid, and as such is entitled to the Right of Soil in and over the said Common Pasture called the Horse Wold> Cow Wold, and Sheep Wold, and the said Common, and Waste Lands, and is entitled in respect of Middle Hill Sheep Walk [hoc. and for facilitating the Mode of proving the several Fails usually required on the passing of such Acts: And whereas the Lands and Grounds of the respective Proprietors in the said Open and Common Fields lie intermixed and dispersed, and the fame and the said Common Pasture, Common and Waste Lands are so circumstanced as to render the Cultivation and Management thereof in their present State inconvenient, and it would tend greatly to the Advantage of the several Proprietors thereof and all Persons interested therein, if the said Open and Common Fields, and Common Pasture, Lanes, or Common and Waste Lands, were divided and inclosed, and specific Parts thereof allotted to the several Persons interested therein, in Proportion to their respective Rights and‘interests,'and a Satisfaction made for the Tythes arising within the Township of Middleton aforesaid; but such beneficial, Purposes cannot be effected without the Aid and Authority of Parliament: May it therefore please Your Majesty that it may be enacted; and be it enacted by the King's most Excellent Majesty, by and with the Advice and Consent of the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and Commons, in this present Parliament assembled, and by the Authority of the same, That William Dawson of Tadcaster in the County of York, "John Lee of Enholmts in the Parish of Patrington in the same County, and John Dickinson of Beverley Park in the Parish of Saint John of Beverley in the same County, Gentlemen, and their Successors to be appointed in Manner herein after mentioned, shall be and they are hereby appointed Commissioners foT dividing and allotting all the Open and Common Fields and Common Pasture, Lanes, or Common and Waste Lands, within the Township of Middleton aforesaid, and for carrying the several other Purposes of this Act into Execution, subject to the Regulations of the said former Act, except in such Cases where the same are hereby varied or altered; and that all Acts, Matters, and Things done by any Two of the said Commissioners, shall be to all Intents and Purposes binding and conclusive, and equally valid and effectual, as if the fame were transaded by all the said Commissioners: Provided nevertheless, that all the said Coin-missioners shall be present on making the Valuation, Division, and Allotment under or by virtue of this or the said former Act.

GEORGII III. REGIS.

Cap. 80.

An Act for dividing and inclosing the several Open Fields, Commons, and Waste Grounds, within the Manor and Township of Clifford, in the West Riding of the County of York. [nth June 1803.]

WHEREAS there are within the Manor and Township of Clifford, in the West Riding of the County of York, several Open Arable Fields, containing together, by Estimation, Three hundred and seventy-five Acres or thereabouts; and certain Commons or Wades called Clifford Moor and Grange Moor, containing together by Edimation, Four hundred and sixty Acres, or thereabouts: And whereas Sir Thomas Gascoigne Baronet, is Lord of the Manor of Clifford aforesaid, and entitled to the Soil of all the said Commons and Waste Grounds, and to all the Royalties belonging to the said Manor: And whereas the said Sir ‘Thomas Gascoigne, James Fox Esquire, Richard Thompson Esquire, and several other Persons are Owners and Proprietors of Messuages and Cottages, or Scites of Messuages and Cottages, Lands, and Grounds within the said Manor of Clifford, and entitled to Right of Common upon the said Commons and Waste Grounds, and to Right of Average in the said Fields, or some Part ['Loc. Cap. 82.

An Act for dividing, allotting, inclodng, and otherwise improving several Commons, Moors, or Wastes, within the Manor of Alston otherwise Alston Moor and Garragill, in the Parish of Alston, and County of Cumberland. [nth June 1803.]

WHEREAS there are within the Manor of AiHon otherwise Alston Moor and Garragill, and within the Parish of Alston, in the County of Cumberland, (exclusive of the Hamlet or Did rift of Prior[dale, and of the Difbift commonly called Gilderfdale Forest or Gilderfdale Pasture, within the same Manor and Parish), certain large Commons, Moors, or Wastes, which in various Parts thereof are called or known by several distinct Names, but which are most commonly called or known by the general Name of Alston Moor Commons, containing together, by Estimation, Twenty thousand Acres or thereabouts: And whereas the Commissioners and Governors of the Royal Hospital for Seamen at Greenwich, in the County of Kent, are Lords of the Laid Manor of Alston otherwise Alston Moor and Garragill, and as such are seised of or entitled to the Soil and Inheritance of, and the [Lee. & Perj\ 16 X Mines,

And be it further enacted, That the said Commissioners shall cause Notice to be given in the Parish Church of Castle Bytham aforesaid, on some Sunday immediately after Divine Service, or by Writing, to be affixed on One of the principal outer Doors of the said Church, and also by Adveitisement to be inferred in the Newspaper called The Lincoln, Rutland, and Stamford Mercury, or in some other Newspaper published or generally circulating in the said County of Lincoln, of the Time and Place of their Full and every other Meeting for the Execution of this Act, at leafs Seven Days before any such Meeting shall be held (Meetings by Adjournment only and always excepted), and that the said Commissioners shall and may adjourn from Time to Time, and from Place to Place, as they shall see Occasion, for the further Execution of this Act; and in case Two Commissioners shall not meet at the Time and Place appointed for any Meeting, or to which any Meeting shall be adjourned, it shall be lawful for any One of the said Commissioners present at such Time and Place, or for the Clerk to the said Commissioners, to adjourn the said Meeting to be held on any future Day, not exceeding Twenty-one Days from the Day of Adjournment, at the fame or any other Place, and the Commissioners or C'erk making such Adjournment, is hertby required to give Notice thereof in Writing to the absent Commissioners.

And be it further enacted, That all other Notices necessary or requisite to be made and given by the said Commissioners, shall be so made and given by Writing to be affixed on the principal outer Door of the said Parish Church, or by Adveriisement to be inserted in the said Newspaper called The Lincoln, Rutland, and Stamford Mercury, or some other Newspaper circulated in the said County of Lincoln.

VII. And be it further enacted, That if any Dispute or Difference shall arise between any of the Proprietors of or Persons interested or claiming to be interested in any of the Lands, Grounds, or other Hereditaments intended to be divided and allotted by this Act, or touching or concerning any of their Rights or Interests therein, it shall be lawful for the said Commissioners, and they are hereby required and authorized to hear, adjudge, and determine such Dispute or Difference, both as to the Ferlon or Perfor.s to whom the Allotment shall be made, and as to the Specification of the Lands or Hereditaments about which such Dispute or Difference shall arise, and what the Allotment or Allotments in lieu of such Lands or Hereditaments should be, and every such Determination shall be binding and conclusive upon all Persons whomsoever, so far as it specifies such Lands or Hereditaments, and fixes what the Allotment or Allotments shall be in lieu thereof; but no such Determination of the said Commissioners, as to the Person or Persons to whom they shall award any such Allotment or Allotments shall exclude Persons who shall deem themselves injured by such Determination, from asserting and trying their Rights at Law or in Equity, in respect of the Title to any such Allotment or Allotments, so that no Trial or Judgement thereupon shall suspend or impede the Execution of this Act for any other Purpose: Provided always, that nothing herein contained shall authorize the said Commissioners to determine the Title to any Messuages, Cottages, Lands, or Hereditaments whatsoever.

VIII. Provided always, and be it further enacted, That upon the Hearing and Determination of any such Disputes or Difference by the said Commissioners, it shall be lawful for them, and they are hereby empowered upon Application to them for that Purpose to settle, afiefs, and award such Colts, Charges, and Expences, as they shall think reasonable to be paid to the Party or Parties in whose Favour any such Dispute or Difference shall be determined to be paid by the Party or Parties whose Claim or Claims, Objection or Objections, shall be disallowed or overruled; and such Costs, Charges, and Expences shall and may be levied and recovered in such and the like Manner, and by such and the like Ways and Means, as the Charges and Expences of obtaining and executing this Act are hereby directed to be levied and recovered.

XXVI. Provided nevertheless, and be it further enacted, That if the Owners or Proprietors of any such old Inclosures, not having any or sufficient Land in the said Lands and Grounds within the said Parishes of Little Kimble and Ellejborough, hereby directed to be divided, allotted, and inclosed, to exonerate their Messuages, Tenements, Gardens, Orchards, Homesteads, Homeclofes, and old Inclosures from Payment of Tythes in Kind as aforesaid, shall be desirous of having a Part of such old Inclosures, assigned or set apart to exonerate the fame Messuages, Tenements, Gardens, Orchards, Homesteads, Homeclofes, and old Inclosures from the Payment of Tythes in Kind, it shall be lawful for the said Commissioners, and they are hereby authorized and empowered, with the Consent of the Proprietors or Owners in Fee or in Tail, or for Life, in Possession of such old Inclosures, to deduct and set out so much and such Part and Parts of such old Inclosures, as shall be equal in Value to the Tythes, both Great and Small, payable by the Owner or Owners of such old Inclosures, in respect of his, her, or their respective Messuages, Tenements, Gardens, Orchards, Homesteads, Homeclofes, and old Inclosures within the said Parishes of Little Kimble and Ellejborough, which Part or Parts of such old Inclosures so deducted and set apart, shall be considered as Part of the Lands and Grounds hereby directed to be divided, allotted, and inclosed, and shall be divided, allotted, and inclosed accordingly as Part thereof; and such Deductions shall be for ever thereafter deemed, taken, and considered to be a full Satisfaction for and Discharge from the Payment of such Tythes.

XXVII. Provided always, and be it further enacted, That until the Execution of the Award of the said Commissioners, or until such other previous Time as the said Commissioners shall, by Writing under their Hands, direct or appoint, the said George John Earl Spencer, William Chapman, Richard Wells, and Joseph Wells, and the other Impropriators, shall severally be entitled to, and shall have, receive, and enjoy all their respective Tythes, in such Manner as they respectively could or might have had, received, and enjoyed the fame, in case this Act had not been made.

XXVIII. Provided also, and be it further enacted, That the several Beech, Box, and other Woods and Wood Lands, lying and being within the said several Parishes, shall respectively remain and continue subject and liable to the Payment of such Tythes as the fame Woods and Wood Lands would respectively have been subject and liable to in case this Act had not been-made.
